children.title: Symretope Relaxation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Group-level representative polytopes and tractable relaxations.

children.title: Symretope Families
children.top_down_role: Group-level polytopes selecting representatives from symmetry orbits.

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(G\) acts on a finite set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
A total order \(\preceq\) is fixed on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The associated symretope is \(S(X,G,\preceq):=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in X:x\preceq gx\ \forall g\in G\}\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of canonical feasible points.

review_flags: Symretope terminology is specialized, and none of the supplied locators supports its precise published definition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hulls of order-canonical binary representatives for finite group actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite binary set \(X\), a finite group action \(G\curvearrowright X\), and a total order \(\preceq\), define the canonical subset \(X^{\mathrm{can}}:=\{x\in X:x\preceq gx\text{ for every }g\in G\}\). The corresponding symretope is
\[
S(X,G,\preceq):=\operatorname{conv}(X^{\mathrm{can}}).
\]
A symretope family is obtained by varying \(X\), \(G\), or the representative order within a specified model class. Its integer points are precisely the canonical feasible binary points, and linear optimization over it searches one chosen representative from each orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symretope is the convex hull of the order-canonical feasible binary points under a specified finite symmetry-group action.
knowledge_statements.title: Symretope Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-hull construction is internally coherent, but "symretope" is specialized terminology and no source establishes that the proposed definition or the stated family parameters match its published meaning.

children.title: Relaxed-Symretope Families
children.top_down_role: Tractable relaxations retaining selected geometric features of symretopes.

assumptions_latex: \(S(X,G,\preceq)\) is a symretope contained in a base relaxation \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The chosen inequalities are valid for every canonical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A relaxed symretope \(R\) satisfies \(S(X,G,\preceq)\subseteq R\subseteq P\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral outer approximation of the symretope.

review_flags: No supplied source establishes the intended relaxed-symretope hierarchy or its naming convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer approximations retaining valid canonicalization inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S(X,G,\preceq)\subseteq P\) be an exact symretope and a base continuous relaxation. A relaxed symretope is a tractable polyhedron \(R\) satisfying
\[
S(X,G,\preceq)\subseteq R\subseteq P.
\]
Typically \(R\) is formed by adding a selected subset of valid representative-selection inequalities to \(P\). A family \((R_k)_{k\in K}\) is a relaxation hierarchy when stronger indices give nested sets, so that \(S(X,G,\preceq)\subseteq R_{k'}\subseteq R_k\subseteq P\) whenever \(k'\) is declared stronger than \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed symretope is a tractable polyhedral outer approximation of the exact canonical-representative hull, often organized as a nested hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Symretope Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusions describe a generic polyhedral outer approximation, but no source establishes the term "relaxed symretope" or the intended hierarchy and strength indexing. The exact specialized definition therefore remains unreliable.

children.title: Symretope Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Geometric distinctions between exact representative polytopes and their relaxed counterparts.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq R\) are nonempty compact relaxations for the same minimization model.
The objective is linear with coefficient vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additive relaxation gap is \(\Delta_R(c):=\min_{x\in S}c^\top x-\min_{x\in R}c^\top x\ge 0\).

notation.meaning: Additive minimization gap in direction c.

review_flags: The gap definition is standard for nested relaxations, but no supplied locator treats symretope relaxation gaps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-dependent additive gaps between exact and relaxed symretopes for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty compact sets \(S
\subseteq R\) and a minimization direction \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
\Delta_R(c):=\min_{x\in S}c^\top x-
\min_{x\in R}c^\top x.
\]
Because \(R\) contains \(S\), one has \(\Delta_R(c)\ge 0\). The relaxation is exact in direction \(c\) precisely when \(\Delta_R(c)=0\). For a normalized objective class \(\mathcal{C}\), the worst-case additive gap is \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal{C}}\Delta_R(c)\); normalization is necessary because positive scaling of \(c\) scales the additive gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symretope relaxation gap is the exact canonical-hull optimum minus the relaxed optimum; it is nonnegative and depends on the objective direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Symretope Relaxation Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed additive gap and its nonnegativity are correct for compact nested minimization sets, but the record primarily defines a gap rather than stating a property, so definition is the more appropriate content kind. No source connects this generic gap construction to symretope relaxation gaps.

children.title: Symresack Family
children.top_down_role: Representative polytopes associated with individual permutations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is invariant under a permutation \(\pi\) of the coordinates.

The lexicographic order uses coordinates \(1,
\ldots,n\) in that order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symresack is \(\operatorname{conv}\{x\in X:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\pi(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Vector obtained by permuting coordinates of x.

review_flags: Symresack terminology and orientation require a specialized source absent from the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic representative polytope associated with one coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi\) be a coordinate permutation satisfying \(\pi(X)=X\). With coordinates inspected in the fixed order \(1,
\ldots,n\), the symresack associated with \(X\) and \(\pi\) is
\[
\operatorname{Symresack}(X,
\pi):=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in X:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\pi(x)\}.
\]
The inequality direction fixes the convention that \(x\) is the lexicographically maximal member of the pair comparison \(\{x,
\pi(x)\}\). For a permutation of order greater than two, this single comparison need not make \(x\) maximal over its entire cyclic orbit unless comparisons with additional powers of \(\pi\) are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symresack is the convex hull of feasible binary vectors lexicographically no smaller than their image under one specified coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.title: Symresack Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required to confirm the standard symresack domain, lexicographic orientation, and whether the term applies to the hull restricted by an arbitrary invariant feasible set \(X\). The higher-order permutation caveat is plausible but likewise unsupported.

children.title: Orbisack Family
children.top_down_role: Representative polytopes specialized to involutive column exchanges.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{m\times 2}\) is invariant under exchanging its two columns.

Rows are compared in the fixed order \(1,
\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The orbisack is \(\operatorname{conv}\{x\in X:x_{\bullet 1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\bullet 2}\}\).

notation.meaning: First column of the binary matrix.
Second column of the binary matrix.

review_flags: The standard orbisack definition requires confirmation from a specialized source not present in the supplied inventory hints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary representative polytope for the involution exchanging two columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{m\times 2}\) be invariant under the involution \(\tau\) that exchanges its two columns. The associated orbisack is
\[
\operatorname{Orbisack}(X):=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in X:x_{\bullet 1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\bullet 2}\}.
\]
Every orbit \(\{x,
\tau(x)\}\) has exactly one matrix satisfying the displayed order, except that a fixed point with identical columns already equals its exchanged image. Hence the selected binary matrices constitute one representative per orbit of the two-column exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orbisack is the convex hull of binary two-column matrices whose first column is lexicographically no smaller than the second.
knowledge_statements.title: Orbisack Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-column lexicographic representative construction is coherent, but a specialized source must confirm the standard orbisack definition and whether an arbitrary exchange-invariant subset \(X\) may be built into that definition rather than treated as an additional model intersection.

children.title: Orbitope Family
children.top_down_role: Representative polytopes for lexicographically ordered binary matrices under column permutations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Packing and Partitioning Orbitopes — Kaibel and Pfetsch
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Packing and Partitioning Orbitopes — Kaibel and Pfetsch

children.title: Full Orbitopes
children.top_down_role: Orbitopes without row-cardinality specialization.

assumptions_latex: \(n,q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\).
The symmetric group \(S_q\) acts on \(\{0,1\}^{n\times q}\) by permuting columns.
Lexicographic order compares columns from row \(1\) through row \(n\), with \(1>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,q}\) contains exactly the convex combinations of lexicographically maximal representatives of column-permutation orbits.

notation.meaning: Full orbitope for binary matrices with column-permutation symmetry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary full orbitope under the complete column-permutation group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,q}:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times q}:x_{\star 1}\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\star 2}\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\star q}\}\). The full orbitope is \[O^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,q}:=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(X^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,q}\bigr).\] Thus no row-cardinality restriction is imposed; the inequalities selecting representatives arise solely from requiring the columns to be lexicographically nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full orbitope is the convex hull of all binary matrices whose columns are arranged in lexicographically nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Orbitopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Full Orbitopes container, and the notation and binary column-permutation scope are precise. No inspectable source with a section, definition, theorem, or page locator is supplied for the specialized orbitope terminology.

children.title: Packing Orbitopes
children.top_down_role: Orbitopes aligned with row-wise packing structure.

assumptions_latex: \(n,q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\).
Columns are interchangeable under the action of \(S_q\).
Lexicographic order uses row order \(1,\ldots,n\) and \(1>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O^{\le}_{n,q}\) is the symmetry-representative polytope for binary row-packing matrices with interchangeable columns.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary packing orbitope with at most one selected column per row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[X^{\le}_{n,q}:=\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times q}:\sum_{j=1}^{q}x_{ij}\le 1\ \text{for every }i,\quad x_{\star 1}\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\star q}\right\}.\] The packing orbitope is \[O^{\le}_{n,q}:=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(X^{\le}_{n,q}\bigr).\] It is the restriction of the full orbitope to matrices satisfying the row-wise packing constraints \(x\mathbf 1\le\mathbf 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The packing orbitope is the convex hull of lexicographically ordered binary matrices having at most one 1 in each row.
knowledge_statements.title: Packing Orbitopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-hull definition correctly specializes to binary matrices with at most one 1 per row, and definition is the appropriate content kind. A specialized orbitope source is required to support the terminology and the asserted relationship to the full orbitope.

children.title: Partitioning Orbitopes
children.top_down_role: Orbitopes aligned with row-wise partitioning structure.

assumptions_latex: \(n,q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\).
Columns are interchangeable under the action of \(S_q\).
Lexicographic order uses row order \(1,\ldots,n\) and \(1>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O^{=}_{n,q}\) is the symmetry-representative polytope for binary row-partitioning matrices with interchangeable columns.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary partitioning orbitope with exactly one selected column per row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[X^{=}_{n,q}:=\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times q}:\sum_{j=1}^{q}x_{ij}=1\ \text{for every }i,\quad x_{\star 1}\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}x_{\star q}\right\}.\] The partitioning orbitope is \[O^{=}_{n,q}:=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(X^{=}_{n,q}\bigr).\] Equivalently, it is the face of the packing orbitope determined by the equations \(x\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partitioning orbitope is the convex hull of lexicographically ordered binary matrices having exactly one 1 in every row.
knowledge_statements.title: Partitioning Orbitopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, row-partitioning condition, and face relationship to the packing orbitope are mathematically coherent and fit the terminal container. No specialized source with an inspectable locator is provided.

children.title: Covering-Orbitope Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural limits distinguishing covering analogues from packing and partitioning cases.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\) and \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 2}\).
The covering representative set consists of binary matrices satisfying \(\sum_{j=1}^{q}x_{ij}\ge 1\) in every row and having lexicographically nonincreasing columns.
The affine complement-and-reversal map is \(y_{ij}=1-x_{i,q-j+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map yields the standard row-packing bound only for \(q=2\); for \(q\ge 3\), it instead yields the weaker bound \(\sum_{j=1}^{q}y_{ij}\le q-1\).

notation.meaning: Covering representative set with lexicographically nonincreasing columns.
Complemented matrix with reversed column order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine boundary separating covering orbitopes from standard row-packing orbitopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^{\ge}_{n,q}\) be the set of matrices \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times q}\) whose columns are lexicographically nonincreasing and which satisfy \(\sum_{j=1}^{q}x_{ij}\ge 1\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For \(x\in X^{\ge}_{n,q}\), define \(y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times q}\) by \(y_{ij}:=1-x_{i,q-j+1}\). The columns of \(y\) are lexicographically nonincreasing, and its row constraints are \[\sum_{j=1}^{q}y_{ij}\le q-1\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.\] When \(q=2\), this is the standard row-packing constraint. When \(q\ge 3\), it permits more than one 1 in a row and therefore does not produce the standard packing orbitope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing entries and reversing the column order transforms each covering-row constraint into a row-cardinality bound of q−1. This is the standard packing bound only when q is two.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering-Orbitope Boundary

children.title: Polyhedral Enforcement Routes
children.top_down_role: Representation and enforcement routes for symmetry-handling polytopes.

children.title: Facet-Inequality Description System
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral description families for symmetry-handling polytopes.

children.title: Facet Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Facet classes associated with symmetry-handling polytopes.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a full-dimensional polytope.
\(K\) is a finite index set, and \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system represents \(P\) irredundantly as the intersection of supporting halfspaces, one for each indexed facet.

notation.meaning: The face induced by the kth supporting inequality.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard facet-description characterization for full-dimensional polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional polyhedral formulation of symmetry-representative geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite system indexed by \(K\) is an irredundant facet description of \(P\) when \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\text{ for every }k\in K\},\] every face \[F_k:=\{x\in P:a_k^{\mathsf T}x=b_k\}\] has dimension \(d-1\), and deleting any indexed inequality strictly enlarges the represented set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An irredundant facet description represents a full-dimensional polytope by supporting halfspaces whose equality faces are facets, with every indexed inequality necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet Descriptions

children.title: Valid-Inequality Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Non-facet or aggregated inequality families supporting representative selection.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty.
The proposed description is a family \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\), indexed by \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The described relaxation contains \(P\), and it equals \(P\) exactly when the valid family is complete.

notation.meaning: Relaxation defined by the stated valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid linear inequalities used to describe or relax a representative polytope.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\), indexed by \(k\in K\), is a valid-inequality description for \(P\) when \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\) holds for every \(x\in P\) and every \(k\in K\). It defines the relaxation \[Q:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\ \text{for all }k\in K\},\] for which \(P\subseteq Q\). The description is exact precisely when \(Q=P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid inequalities contain the target polytope in their intersection; they form an exact description only when that intersection equals the polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Inequality Descriptions

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Description Completeness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between complete polyhedral descriptions and partial inequality systems.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a polytope.
\(K\) is an index set, with \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(k\in K\).
Every inequality \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\) is valid for \(P\), and \(Q_K:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\text{ for every }k\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is complete for \(P\) exactly when every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus P\) violates at least one inequality indexed by \(K\); relative completeness over \(R\supseteq P\) requires this only for \(x\in R\setminus P\).

notation.meaning: Intersection of the selected valid halfspaces.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard exactness criterion for valid-inequality systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criteria for finite or infinite valid-inequality families, globally or relative to a specified relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The valid-inequality family indexed by \(K\) is complete for \(P\) if and only if \[P=Q_K.\] Equivalently, it is complete if and only if \[\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus P\text{ there exists }k\in K\text{ such that }a_k^{\mathsf T}x>b_k.\] Given a specified relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) with \(P\subseteq R\), the family is complete relative to \(R\) if and only if \[P=R\cap Q_K,\] equivalently, if every \(x\in R\setminus P\) violates at least one inequality indexed by \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid-inequality family is globally complete exactly when it excludes every point outside the target polytope. It is complete relative to a relaxation when it excludes every point of that relaxation lying outside the target polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Description Completeness Regimes

children.title: Separation-Propagation Enforcement Coupling
children.top_down_role: Implicit enforcement through cut separation and domain propagation.

children.title: Symmetry-Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Implicit enforcement through identification of violated symmetry-handling inequalities.

assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is the current relaxation.
\(P\subseteq R\) is the symmetry-representative polytope.
\(\mathcal C\) is a family of inequalities valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a violated symmetry cut or a certificate that no inequality in \(\mathcal C\) is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic separation oracle for a specified family of symmetry inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a point \(\bar x\in R\). Search the indexed family \(\mathcal C=\{a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k:k\in K\}\) for an index satisfying \(a_k^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_k\). If one exists, output such an inequality as a symmetry cut and replace the relaxation by \(R\cap\{x:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\}\). Otherwise output the certificate \[a_k^{\mathsf T}\bar x\le b_k\quad\text{for every }k\in K.\] This certificate concerns only the designated family \(\mathcal C\), unless that family is complete for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry-cut separator either finds a violated valid symmetry inequality at the current point or certifies that none in the chosen family is violated.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, and the family-relative certificate is carefully limited rather than being overstated as membership in the representative polytope. No inspectable symmetry-specific separation source is supplied.

children.title: Symmetry-Aware Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction derived from representative restrictions or symmetry-handling geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(D=\prod_{r=1}^{m}D_r\) is the current finite variable domain.
A symmetry-breaking constraint system \(S\) is required of all retained solutions.
Propagation preserves every point in \(D\cap S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At a fixed point, each retained value has support in \(D\cap S\), so pruning is sound and symmetry-aware.

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of current variable domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain propagation induced by an exact symmetry-breaking constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D\), apply a monotone contracting operator \(\Phi_S\) satisfying \[D\cap S\subseteq\Phi_S(D)\subseteq D.\] Iterate \(D^{t+1}:=\Phi_S(D^t)\) from \(D^0:=D\) until \(D^{t+1}=D^t\), and output the fixed-point domains. For domain consistency, delete \(v\in D_r\) exactly when no \(x\in D\cap S\) satisfies \(x_r=v\). The resulting deletions cannot remove a feasible representative satisfying \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetry-aware propagation repeatedly removes domain values unsupported by the symmetry-breaking constraints while preserving every feasible representative.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Aware Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes a sound finite-domain propagation algorithm and distinguishes general sound contraction from domain-consistency deletion. It fits the propagation leaf, but the specialized symmetry-propagation claims lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Integrated Polyhedral Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Coordination of separation-based enforcement with propagation-based enforcement.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq R^0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), where \(P\) is the representative polytope.
Each generated cut is valid for \(P\).
Each propagation operator preserves all feasible representatives in its input domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iteration preserves \(P\), while the relaxation and variable domains can only contract.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating cut separation and symmetry-aware domain propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((R^0,D^0)\). At iteration \(t\), separate a valid symmetry cut \(C^t\) at the current relaxation solution and set \(R^{t+1}:=R^t\cap C^t\); if no cut is found, leave \(R^{t+1}:=R^t\). Then propagate the symmetry-breaking system over \(D^t\) to obtain \(D^{t+1}\subseteq D^t\). Stop when neither component changes. Validity and propagation soundness imply \[P\subseteq R^{t+1}\subseteq R^t\quad\text{and}\quad P\cap D^t\subseteq D^{t+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrated enforcement alternates valid symmetry cuts with sound domain propagation until neither the relaxation nor the variable domains become tighter.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Polyhedral Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating separation-and-propagation procedure fits the algorithm container, and its contraction and preservation claims follow from the explicitly stated validity and soundness assumptions. No source with a specific locator supports this integrated enforcement formulation.

children.title: Compact-Extended Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Original-space and lifted representations of canonical matrix structures.

children.title: Compact Representations
children.top_down_role: Original-space or low-auxiliary representations of symmetry-handling structures.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a polytope.
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax\le b\) is compact when it directly represents \(P\) with polynomially many explicitly encoded inequalities.

notation.meaning: Target representative polytope in the original variables.
Direct formulation in the original variable space.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard direct polyhedral formulation terminology
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct polynomial-size descriptions in the original variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compact representation of \(P\) is a direct linear description \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\le b\}\] whose number of rows and total encoding length are polynomial in the chosen combinatorial input size. It introduces no auxiliary variables. Compactness is relative to the encoding family and does not follow merely from the finiteness of a facet description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact representation describes the target polytope directly in its original variables using polynomially many explicitly encoded inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Representations

children.title: Representation-Size Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares direct and lifted polyhedral descriptions of a symmetry-restricted representative set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a symmetry-restricted polytope. A direct formulation \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) has size equal to its numbers of inequalities and variables. An extended formulation is \(Q=\{(x,y):Cx+Dy\le d\}\) with \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). Introducing auxiliary variables may reduce the number of inequalities, even when every direct description of \(P\) is large; projection can conversely create many inequalities. Thus formulation size must report both the inequality count and the total variable count, together with the projection map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifting may replace a large direct inequality system by fewer inequalities and more variables; meaningful size comparisons report both counts and the projection.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a polytope.
\(Q\) projects exactly onto \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), while the direct and extended descriptions may have substantially different inequality and variable counts.

children.title: Lex-Leader Formulations
children.top_down_role: Static representative restrictions based on lexicographic comparison.

children.title: Complete-Group Lex Leaders
children.top_down_role: Lexicographic systems indexed by the full acting group.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Group Lex Leaders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-group lexicographic representative system for a finite permutation action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq D^n\), where \(D\) is totally ordered, and let a finite group \(G\leq S_n\) preserve \(X\). Fix the induced lexicographic order \(\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\) on \(D^n\). The complete-group lex-leader set is \[L_G=\{x\in X:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}g(x)\text{ for every }g\in G\}.\] Every orbit \(Gx\) contains exactly one distinct vector in \(L_G\), namely its lexicographically maximal vector. Hence optimizing a \(G\)-invariant objective over \(L_G\) preserves the attainable objective values over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imposing a lex comparison against every group element retains exactly the lexicographically maximal vector from each orbit and preserves invariant optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is totally ordered and \(X\subseteq D^n\).
\(G\leq S_n\) is finite and satisfies \(g(X)=X\) for every \(g\in G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_G\cap Gx\) contains exactly one distinct vector for every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and one-distinct-vector-per-orbit conclusion are mathematically standard and fit the complete-group leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the claims.

children.title: Restricted Lex-Leader Family
children.top_down_role: Restricted lexicographic systems built from selected generators or subgroups.

children.title: Generator Lex Leaders
children.top_down_role: Lexicographic representative restrictions derived from selected group generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Lex Leaders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted lex comparisons indexed only by a chosen generating set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the setting of complete-group lex leaders, let \(S\subseteq G\) generate \(G\). The generator lex-leader condition is \[x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}s(x)\qquad\text{for every }s\in S.\] Its feasible set \(L_S\) contains \(L_G\), because every complete lex leader satisfies each generator comparison. In general, closure of \(S\) under composition does not make these individual inequalities imply comparisons with all products in \(G\); consequently \(L_S\) may contain multiple distinct vectors from one orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Comparisons with group generators are valid but generally weaker than comparisons with every group element, so several representatives of one orbit may remain.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on \(X\subseteq D^n\) by coordinate permutations.
\(S\subseteq G\) generates \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_G\subseteq L_S\), but equality need not hold.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generator-indexed condition fits the leaf and the inclusion L_G subseteq L_S is correct, but the asserted failure of full-orbit coverage requires a relevant source with a specific locator.

children.title: Subgroup Lex Leaders
children.top_down_role: Lexicographic representative restrictions derived from selected subgroups.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgroup Lex Leaders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic representatives formed with respect to a selected subgroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\leq G\) be a subgroup acting on the \(G\)-invariant set \(X\subseteq D^n\). The subgroup lex-leader set is \[L_H=\{x\in X:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}h(x)\text{ for every }h\in H\}.\] Each \(H\)-orbit has exactly one distinct lexicographically maximal member in \(L_H\). Moreover \(L_G\subseteq L_H\). Unless \(H\) induces the same orbits as \(G\) on \(X\), different \(H\)-orbit leaders belonging to one \(G\)-orbit can survive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgroup comparisons choose one leader per subgroup orbit, but may retain several points from a larger full-group orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq D^n\) with \(D\) totally ordered.
\(H\leq G\) and both groups preserve \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(H\)-orbit meets \(L_H\) once, and \(L_G\subseteq L_H\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subgroup lex-leader definition and coverage distinction are precise and locally appropriate, but no citation supports them.

children.title: Lex-Leader Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Symmetry coverage obtained from generator-level, subgroup-level, or broader group restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lex-Leader Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes complete, orbit-complete, and partial lex-leader systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\subseteq G\), define \(L_T=\{x\in X:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}t(x)\text{ for all }t\in T\}\). The system is complete when \(T=G\), orbit-complete on \(X\) when \(L_T=L_G\), and partial when \(L_G\subsetneq L_T\). Orbit-completeness is equivalent to every comparison indexed by \(g\in G\setminus T\) being implied, on \(X\), by the comparisons indexed by \(T\). Completeness of the index set is sufficient but not necessary for orbit-completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted family is orbit-complete exactly when its comparisons imply every omitted group comparison on the feasible set; otherwise it leaves extra representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite symmetry group of \(X\subseteq D^n\).
\(T\subseteq G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_T=L_G\) exactly when all omitted lex comparisons are implied on \(X\); otherwise \(L_G\subsetneq L_T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coverage-regime property is internally consistent and fits the terminal container, but its equivalence and sufficiency claims have no cited source.

children.title: Symresack Constraints
children.top_down_role: Binary lexicographic restrictions associated with a selected permutation action.

knowledge_statements.title: Symresack Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary lex-order polytope associated with one coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\in S_n\) permute the coordinates of binary vectors. The symresack associated with \(\pi\) is \[P_\pi=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\pi(x)\}.\] Symresack constraints are linear inequalities whose common binary solutions satisfy this lexicographic comparison; an exact symresack description has relaxation equal to \(P_\pi\). If \(\pi\) is a symmetry of the underlying model, intersecting its feasible binary set with the comparison retains at least one member of every orbit generated by \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symresack is the convex hull of binary vectors lexicographically no smaller than their image under one coordinate permutation.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\in S_n\) acts by permuting coordinates.
\(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) uses the order \(0<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\pi=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\pi(x)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated binary symresack definition is plausible and fits the leaf, but the specialized terminology, exactness convention, and orbit-retention claim require an authoritative symresack citation.

children.title: Orbisack Constraints
children.top_down_role: Binary matrix restrictions associated with interchangeability of two columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbisack Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-column binary lex-order polytope for column-interchange symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\geq1\), let \(X=(x_{ij})\in\{0,1\}^{p\times2}\). The orbisack is \[O_p=\operatorname{conv}\{X\in\{0,1\}^{p\times2}:X_{\cdot1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot2}\}.\] Orbisack constraints give a linear description or relaxation enforcing this column comparison. When exchanging the two columns preserves the original feasible set and objective, the comparison retains the lexicographically ordered member of each two-column orbit; matrices with identical columns are fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orbisack is the convex hull of binary two-column matrices whose first column is lexicographically at least their second.
assumptions_latex: The relevant symmetry interchanges the two columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(O_p=\operatorname{conv}\{X:X_{\cdot1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot2}\}\).

notation.meaning: nonincreasing lexicographic order down the rows

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-column binary convex-hull definition is appropriate for an orbisack, but the named construction and formulation claims lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Binary Lex-Constraint Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural distinctions governing applicability of symresack or orbisack constraint families.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Lex-Constraint Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and completeness limits of binary lexicographic symmetry-breaking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Binary lex constraints preserve an optimization problem only when each indexed permutation maps the feasible set to itself and leaves the objective invariant. Even under validity, comparisons for a proper subset \(T\subsetneq G\) need not isolate one point per \(G\)-orbit. Moreover, polyhedral descriptions specialized to \(\{0,1\}^n\) do not automatically describe the convex hull for general integer domains. Thus removing model symmetry, full coverage, or binarity respectively can cause loss of optima, residual symmetry, or loss of formulation exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lex constraints can remove optima without genuine symmetry, leave residual symmetry under partial coverage, and lose exactness outside binary domains.
assumptions_latex: Lex comparisons are imposed for permutations in \(T\).
The specialized formulation was derived for \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity requires symmetry; one-per-orbit coverage requires \(L_T=L_G\); binary-polyhedral exactness need not extend to larger integer domains.

notation.meaning: feasible set after the restricted comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but saying preservation occurs only under feasible-set symmetry and objective invariance is too strong: those conditions provide a general symmetry-based guarantee but are not logically necessary for accidental preservation of an optimum. A source is needed to establish the intended corrected boundary.

children.title: Column-Ordering Formulations
children.top_down_role: Direct representative restrictions based on ordered columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Ordering Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct lexicographic restriction for models invariant under arbitrary column permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in D^{p\times q}\), with \(D\) totally ordered, and suppose \(S_q\) acts by permuting columns while preserving feasibility and objective values. The column-ordering condition is \[X_{\cdot1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot2}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\cdot q}.\] Every column-permutation orbit contains an ordered matrix obtained by sorting its columns. The ordered matrix is unique as a matrix; permutations among equal columns do not create a distinct matrix. Hence this restriction gives one distinct representative per orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorting interchangeable columns in nonincreasing lexicographic order yields one distinct matrix from every column-permutation orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is totally ordered.
All permutations of the \(q\) columns preserve feasibility and objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(S_q\)-orbit contains exactly one distinct matrix satisfying the column-ordering condition.

notation.meaning: symmetric group acting on the columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The column-ordering condition and uniqueness of the sorted matrix are mathematically coherent and fit the formulation leaf, but no orbitope or symmetry source is cited.

children.title: Shifted-Column Inequality Formulations
children.top_down_role: Named inequality systems for packing and partitioning orbitopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Shifted-Column Inequality Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet-strengthening systems for binary packing and partitioning orbitopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be a packing or partitioning orbitope: the convex hull of lexicographically nonincreasing binary matrices having, respectively, at most or exactly one entry equal to one in each row. A shifted-column inequality has the form \[x(B)\leq x(S),\] where \(B\) is an admissible row suffix, called a bar, and \(S\) is the corresponding shifted column in the triangular orbitope index set. Together with variable bounds and the appropriate row-sum equations or inequalities, the full shifted-column family describes \(O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shifted-column inequalities compare a row suffix with a compatible shifted column and, with row constraints and bounds, describe packing or partitioning orbitopes.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is a binary matrix indexed by the triangular orbitope positions.
Rows have at most one one in the packing case or exactly one in the partitioning case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full shifted-column system, bounds, and row constraints yield the packing or partitioning orbitope \(O\).

notation.meaning: sum of entries indexed by U
shifted column compatible with the bar

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but the notions of admissible bar, corresponding shifted column, and triangular index set are not defined sufficiently to verify the inequality family or its exact-description conclusion without a specialized source.

children.title: Extended Orbitope Formulations
children.top_down_role: Lifted formulations for ordered matrix representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Orbitope Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-flow lift encoding lexicographically ordered binary matrix representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be a packing or partitioning orbitope. Construct an acyclic directed network whose source-to-sink paths encode the boundary between permitted and forbidden entries of a lexicographically ordered binary matrix. Let \(f\) be a unit source-to-sink flow and couple each matrix entry \(x_{ij}\) to the flow arcs permitting that entry. The resulting polyhedron \(Q=\{(x,f):f\text{ is a unit network flow and the coupling constraints hold}\}\) is an extended formulation when \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=O.\] Integrality of the network-flow polytope supports integral ordered representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-flow network can encode ordered binary matrices in auxiliary variables; projecting the coupled flow formulation yields the orbitope.
assumptions_latex: The acyclic network encodes precisely the admissible lex-order boundaries.
Coupling constraints associate matrix entries with their permitted flow states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=O\), so \(Q\) is an extended formulation of the orbitope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A lifted network-flow representation fits the leaf, but the network and coupling inequalities are unspecified, and exactness is stated conditionally through proj_x(Q)=O rather than established for a concrete formulation. A specialized source is required.

children.title: Schreier–Sims Table Cuts
children.top_down_role: Leader-based inequality families organized by stabilizer-chain data.

knowledge_statements.title: Schreier–Sims Table Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary leader inequalities derived from a stabilizer chain and its orbit table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\leq S_n\) act on \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). Choose leaders \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\), and let \(G_{i-1}\) be the pointwise stabilizer of \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{i-1}\). For every \(j\) in the orbit \(G_{i-1}\ell_i\), the Schreier–Sims table cut is \[x_{\ell_i}\geq x_j.\] The family orders each leader against positions reachable while earlier leaders remain fixed. It is valid for the representatives selected recursively by this stabilizer-chain rule, though it need not equal the complete-group lex-leader system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each stabilizer-chain level, the selected binary leader must dominate every coordinate in its orbit under the current stabilizer.
assumptions_latex: \(G\leq S_n\) acts by coordinate permutations on binary vectors.
\(G_{i-1}\) fixes the earlier leaders pointwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\ell_i}\geq x_j\) for every \(j\in G_{i-1}\ell_i\) and every table level \(i\).

notation.meaning: leader coordinate at stabilizer-chain level i
orbit of the current leader under that stabilizer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate for the cut family, but the precise leader convention, stabilizer-chain construction, inequality orientation, and representative-validity claim require an authoritative Schreier–Sims table citation.

children.title: Orbit Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Strong and weak representative inequalities derived from variable orbits.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Inequality Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representative inequalities for one binary-variable orbit under a current stabilizer subgroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be invariant under a permutation group \(H\) acting on variable indices. For an orbit \(O\) of \(H\), fix \(r\in O\). Every \(H\)-orbit of feasible solutions contains a representative satisfying the strong orbit inequalities \[x_r\ge x_j\qquad(j\in O).\] Indeed, when some coordinate in \(O\) equals one, a group element can move such a coordinate to \(r\); when all are zero, the inequalities already hold. The aggregated weak inequality \[|O|x_r\ge\sum_{j\in O}x_j\] follows from the strong family but need not imply it in the linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one binary orbit, a canonical solution may make the chosen representative dominate every orbit member; summing these inequalities gives a weaker aggregate constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is invariant under \(H\).
\(O\) is one orbit of the current stabilizer subgroup \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A representative can satisfy \(x_r\ge x_j\) for all \(j\in O\), implying \(|O|x_r\ge\sum_{j\in O}x_j\).

notation.meaning: Permutation group or current stabilizer acting on variables.
Orbit of binary-variable indices under H.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports orbit inequalities or their stabilizer-qualified formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representative-existence claim and the distinction between the componentwise and aggregated inequalities are plausible, and the principle kind fits the inequality-family container. However, no citation supports the stabilizer-qualified formulation or terminology. The sentences beginning with “Indeed” constitute proof text and must be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Orbital Conflict Cuts
children.top_down_role: Symmetry-derived cut families incorporating conflict structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbital Conflict Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-type inequalities obtained when symmetry orbits expose pairwise conflicts among binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be invariant under a permutation group \(H\), and let the conflict graph have vertex set \([n]\), with \(\{p,q\}\) an edge whenever \(x_p+x_q\le1\) holds for every \(x\in X\). If an orbit \(O\) of a subgroup of \(H\) induces a clique in this graph, then the orbital conflict cut \[\sum_{j\in O}x_j\le1\] is valid for \(X\). More generally, any clique assembled from orbit images of known conflicts yields its corresponding binary clique inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all variables in a symmetry orbit conflict pairwise, at most one can equal one, yielding an orbit-derived clique cut.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
Every distinct pair in \(O\) is a valid conflict pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{j\in O}x_j\le1\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: Orbit inducing a clique in the conflict graph.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically addresses orbital conflict cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique inequality follows from the stated pairwise-conflict hypothesis, and property is a defensible kind for its validity statement. No source establishes that this construction is the intended meaning of “orbital conflict cuts,” and the final generalization about cliques assembled from orbit images is insufficiently defined to verify.

children.title: Problem-Native Symmetry Breaking

children.title: First-Use Activation Order Correspondence

children.title: First-Use Ordering
children.top_down_role: Canonical ordering of interchangeable objects by their earliest modeled use.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Use Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical ordering of interchangeable labels by the first indexed object assigned to each label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of ordered object \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) to interchangeable label \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Define \[f_j=\min\bigl(\{i:x_{ij}=1\}\cup\{m+1\}\bigr).\] The first-use ordering condition is \[f_1\le f_2\le\cdots\le f_q.\] Equivalently, each used label after the first must have a predecessor label used at an earlier object index. Relabeling interchangeable labels by increasing finite first-use index, with unused labels last, produces a representative satisfying this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable labels are numbered by their earliest assigned object, with unused labels placed after all used labels.
assumptions_latex: Objects have the fixed order \(1<\cdots<m\).
Labels \(1,\ldots,q\) are interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical assignment satisfies \(f_1\le\cdots\le f_q\).

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of object i to label j.
First-use index of label j, or m+1 if unused.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not identify a first-use symmetry-breaking formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition matches the terminal container, but no cited source supports it. The claimed equivalence with a predecessor being used at an earlier object index requires an exclusivity assumption such as each object receiving at most one label; otherwise two labels can have the same first-use index while the nondecreasing condition still holds.

children.title: Activation Ordering
children.top_down_role: Canonical ordering of interchangeable objects by activation status or activation position.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prefix activation convention for an indexed family of interchangeable resources or labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For interchangeable resources indexed by \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(y_j\in\{0,1\}\) equal one exactly when resource \(j\) is active. The activation ordering condition is \[y_1\ge y_2\ge\cdots\ge y_q.\] Thus the active set must be a prefix \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\) for some \(k\in\{0,\ldots,q\}\). Because permuting resource indices preserves feasibility and objective value, every solution has an equivalent relabeling satisfying this ordering, provided activation is defined consistently with resource use.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable resources are relabeled so that all active resources form an initial prefix of their index set.
assumptions_latex: Resources \(1,\ldots,q\) are interchangeable.
\(y_j=1\) holds exactly when resource \(j\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A canonical representative satisfies \(y_j\ge y_{j+1}\) for every \(j<q\).

notation.meaning: Binary activation indicator for resource j.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not specifically support activation ordering as symmetry breaking.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The prefix-activation condition is mathematically coherent and condition is the correct role for this leaf. Its symmetry-breaking interpretation nevertheless has no supporting citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: First-Use Activation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which first-use conventions coincide with activation-based ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Use Activation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between ordered first-use indices, activation prefixes, and assignment precedence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_j=\min(\{i:x_{ij}=1\}\cup\{m+1\})\) and impose the exact activation link \[y_j=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_j\le m.\] Then first-use ordering \(f_1\le\cdots\le f_q\) implies activation ordering \(y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_q\). Conversely, activation ordering alone determines only which labels are used; together with the precedence conditions \[x_{ij}\le\sum_{k<i}x_{k,j-1}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m;\ j=2,\ldots,q),\] it enforces increasing first-use indices for all used labels. Hence activation and precedence jointly represent the first-use convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered first uses imply prefix activation; prefix activation becomes equivalent to first-use ordering only when coupled with assignment-precedence constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{ij}\) are binary assignment variables.
\(y_j\) is linked exactly to whether label \(j\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-use ordering implies ordered activation, and ordered activation plus precedence recovers first-use ordering.

notation.meaning: First-use index, with m+1 representing nonuse.
Exact activation indicator for label j.
Assignment of object i to label j.

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports the stated first-use and activation equivalence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the correspondence container, but no source supports the asserted equivalence. To identify the non-strict first-use ordering with the strict precedence system, the record must state the assignment exclusivity assumptions that prevent distinct labels from first occurring at the same object.

children.title: Utilization-Profile Order Family
children.top_down_role: Ordering interchangeable objects through aggregate utilization profiles.

children.title: Load Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering interchangeable objects by aggregate utilization or assignment load.

knowledge_statements.title: Load Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonincreasing total-load convention for interchangeable resources with assignment-dependent loads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) assign item \(i\) to interchangeable resource \(j\), and let \(w_i\ge0\) be the load contributed by item \(i\). Define \[L_j=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i x_{ij}.\] The load-ordering condition is \[L_1\ge L_2\ge\cdots\ge L_q.\] Whenever permuting resource indices preserves all constraints and the objective, sorting resources by nonincreasing load maps every feasible solution to an equivalent representative satisfying these inequalities. Equal loads may leave residual symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable resources are indexed by nonincreasing assigned load; ties may retain symmetry.
assumptions_latex: Resource indices are interchangeable.
Loads satisfy \(w_i\ge0\) and depend only on assigned items.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A symmetry-class representative satisfies \(L_j\ge L_{j+1}\) for every \(j<q\).

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of item i to resource j.
Total load assigned to resource j.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not specifically document load-based symmetry breaking.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The load-sorting condition is precise and appropriately classified as a condition, including the residual-symmetry qualification. No cited source or specific locator supports load ordering as a symmetry-breaking formulation.

children.title: Cardinality Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering interchangeable objects by counts of selected or assigned elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonincreasing assigned-item count for interchangeable resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of item \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) to interchangeable resource \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), and define its cardinality by \[C_j=\sum_{i=1}^m x_{ij}.\] The cardinality-ordering condition is \[C_1\ge C_2\ge\cdots\ge C_q.\] If resource permutations preserve feasibility and objective value, sorting resources by decreasing cardinality yields an equivalent feasible representative satisfying the condition. Resources having equal cardinality remain interchangeable unless a secondary ordering rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable resources are indexed by nonincreasing numbers of assigned items, with ties requiring another rule for fuller symmetry breaking.
assumptions_latex: Assignments are binary.
All resource indices are interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A canonical representative satisfies \(C_j\ge C_{j+1}\) for every \(j<q\).

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of item i to resource j.
Number of items assigned to resource j.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not specifically document cardinality ordering for interchangeable resources.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cardinality-ordering statement is mathematically coherent, matches the leaf, and is correctly typed as a condition. It lacks any source reference or locator supporting its use for interchangeable resources.

children.title: Profile Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering interchangeable objects by structured utilization profiles.

knowledge_statements.title: Profile Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic ordering of multidimensional utilization profiles for interchangeable resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) assign item \(i\) to interchangeable resource \(j\), and let \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) be its ordered attribute vector. Define the utilization profile \[P_j=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i x_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^d.\] Fix the coordinate order and require \[P_1\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}P_2\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}P_q.\] If resource permutations preserve the model, lexicographically sorting the profiles selects an equivalent representative. Identical profiles leave residual symmetry among the corresponding resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable resources are sorted lexicographically by fixed multidimensional utilization profiles; identical profiles may remain symmetric.
assumptions_latex: Resource indices are interchangeable.
The coordinate order defining \(\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A representative satisfies \(P_j\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}P_{j+1}\) for every \(j<q\).

notation.meaning: Ordered attribute vector of item i.
Aggregate utilization profile of resource j.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifies utilization-profile symmetry-breaking inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic profile condition is internally consistent and fits the profile-ordering leaf. No citation supports the formulation or its symmetry-breaking interpretation, so its intended scope cannot be independently checked.

children.title: Representative-Precedence Encoding Interface
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable formulations for canonical object identities and label precedence.

children.title: Representative Encodings
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable encodings that assign canonical identities to interchangeable objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary encoding of the least-indexed object assigned to each interchangeable label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary assignments \(x_{ij}\), introduce \(r_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) with the intended meaning that object \(i\) is the first representative of label \(j\). The equivalence \[r_{ij}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_{ij}=1\ \text{ and }\ x_{kj}=0\ \text{for every }k<i\] is encoded by \[r_{ij}\le x_{ij},\qquad r_{ij}\le1-x_{kj}\ (k<i),\qquad r_{ij}\ge x_{ij}-\sum_{k<i}x_{kj}.\] Thus a used label has exactly one representative, while an unused label has none.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representative variable identifies the least-indexed object assigned to a label and is enforced by exact binary linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Objects are indexed by the fixed order \(1<\cdots<m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities enforce \(r_{ij}=1\) exactly for the first object assigned to label \(j\).

notation.meaning: Assignment of object i to label j.
Indicator that i represents the first use of label j.

review_flags: The encoding is standard but no supplied source locator supports this representative formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary inequalities do encode the stated first-representative indicator, and representation is the correct content kind. The record supplies no source or inspectable locator for this encoding.

children.title: Precedence Encodings
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable encodings that impose canonical label or activation precedence.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment inequalities encoding value precedence among interchangeable labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each ordered object \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) receive one of the interchangeable labels \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), represented by \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\). The inequalities \[x_{ij}\le\sum_{k<i}x_{k,j-1}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m;\ j=2,\ldots,q)\] encode label precedence: an occurrence of label \(j\) is permitted only after an earlier occurrence of label \(j-1\). Consequently, every used label has all lower labels used, and the first-use indices of used labels are strictly increasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A label may occur only after its immediate predecessor has occurred, forcing interchangeable labels into increasing first-use order.
assumptions_latex: Each object receives exactly one label.
Labels are interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities enforce \(f_1<f_2<\cdots<f_k\) for the used-label prefix \(\{1,ldots,k\}\).

notation.meaning: Indicator that object i receives label j.
First index at which label j occurs.

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports value-precedence encoding.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precedence inequalities are plausible and representation fits the terminal container, but no source is cited. In addition, the conclusion contains the malformed text “1,ldots,k” instead of a delimited LaTeX ellipsis, and the endpoint k is not introduced or quantified.

children.title: Representative-Precedence Linking
children.top_down_role: Structural links between canonical identity choices and precedence restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative-Precedence Linking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear links making first representatives obey label precedence and activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_{ij}=1\) exactly when object \(i\) is the first user of label \(j\), and let \(y_j\) indicate whether label \(j\) is active. The interface constraints \[\sum_{i=1}^m r_{ij}=y_j\qquad(j=1,\ldots,q)\] and \[r_{ij}\le\sum_{k<i}r_{k,j-1}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m;\ j=2,\ldots,q)\] link representative and precedence encodings. They ensure that each active label has one representative and that the representative of label \(j-1\) precedes the representative of label \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking equations give each active label one first representative, while precedence links order consecutive labels’ representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(r_{ij}\) is an exact first-representative indicator.
\(y_j\) is an exact label-activation indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Active-label representatives are unique and occur in increasing label order.
review_flags: No supplied source locator documents the representative-precedence interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is suitable for a linking-constraint leaf, and the formulas express the intended interface when the indicators are exact. No source supports this particular formulation, and the binary domains and meanings of m and q should be stated explicitly in a sourced replacement.

children.title: Symmetry-Coverage Regime Family
