children.title: Complete Symmetry Breaking
children.top_down_role: Representative-selection regimes intended to retain one representative per full symmetry orbit.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Symmetry Breaking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact orbit-transversal criterion for a symmetry-breaking restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a group \(G\) act on a feasible set \(X\), with objective value invariant under this action, and let \(R\subseteq X\) be the set retained by added symmetry-breaking constraints. The constraints achieve complete symmetry breaking when \[|R\cap(Gx)|=1\qquad\text{for every }x\in X,\] where \(Gx=\{gx:g\in G\}\). Thus \(R\) is a transversal of the feasible solution orbits: it removes every noncanonical symmetric copy without deleting an entire orbit. Requiring merely \(R\cap(Gx)\ne\varnothing\) preserves an optimum but does not guarantee completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete symmetry breaking retains exactly one feasible solution from every group orbit; retaining one or more representatives is only partial breaking.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on \(X\).
Feasibility and objective value are invariant under \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Completeness is equivalent to \(|R\cap(Gx)|=1\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Orbit of feasible solution x under G.
Feasible points retained after symmetry breaking.
Symmetry group acting on the feasible set.

review_flags: The orbit-transversal definition is standard, but the supplied locators do not specifically address complete symmetry breaking.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orbit-transversal criterion is precise, plain text agrees with the LaTeX, and definition is the correct role for the complete-symmetry-breaking leaf. The candidate nevertheless has no citation or locator supporting this terminology and criterion.

children.title: Partial Symmetry Breaking
children.top_down_role: Restrictions handling selected generators, subgroups, or symmetry classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Symmetry Breaking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbitwise definition for static symmetry-breaking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the feasible integer set and let a finite group \(G\) act on \(X\), preserving the objective. For additional constraints \(S\), write \(X_S=\{x\in X:S(x)\}\). The constraints partially break \(G\)-symmetry if every orbit retains a representative but at least one orbit retains multiple representatives: \[\forall x\in X,\quad (Gx)\cap X_S\ne\varnothing,\qquad \exists y\in X:\ |(Gy)\cap X_S|>1.\] Consequently, if optimization over \(X\) attains an optimum, optimization over \(X_S\) retains an optimum while not selecting a unique representative from every orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial symmetry breaking preserves at least one feasible point from every symmetry orbit but leaves multiple representatives in at least one orbit; when an optimum is attained, an equivalent optimum remains.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts on \(X\).
The objective is constant on every orbit \(Gx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is partial exactly when every orbit meets \(X_S\) and some orbit meets it more than once.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit-representative definition of partial symmetry breaking
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Symmetry-Coverage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Residual equivalence remaining under restricted symmetry-breaking systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Coverage Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-multiplicity boundaries separating unsafe, partial, and complete coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X/G\) denote the set of symmetry orbits and define \(m_S(O)=|O\cap X_S|\) for each \(O\in X/G\). Symmetry-breaking constraints \(S\) are coverage-valid precisely when \(m_S(O)\ge 1\) for every orbit. Within this valid regime they are complete when \(m_S(O)=1\) for every orbit, and partial when \(m_S(O)>1\) for at least one orbit. If \(m_S(O)=0\) for some orbit, \(S\) crosses the validity boundary by deleting that entire orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orbit intersection counts distinguish complete coverage, partial coverage, and invalid symmetry breaking that removes an entire orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on the feasible set \(X\).
\(X_S\subseteq X\) is induced by the added constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary is determined by whether \(m_S(O)\) equals zero, one, or exceeds one.

notation.meaning: number of retained representatives of orbit O

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit-intersection counts characterize symmetry coverage

children.title: Strength-Size Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Comparison of symmetry removal, relaxation geometry, and encoding size.

children.title: Relaxation Strength
children.top_down_role: Geometric strength of relaxations produced by alternative symmetry-breaking formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance comparison for continuous relaxations of equivalent symmetry-breaking formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) be formulations in a common original-variable space \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the projection of the continuous relaxation of \(F_i\). Formulation \(F_1\) is at least as strong as \(F_2\) when \(P_1\subseteq P_2\), and strictly stronger when the inclusion is strict. For \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(v_i(c)=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in P_i\}\). Whenever both values are finite, \[P_1\subseteq P_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_1(c)\ge v_2(c).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation has a stronger relaxation when its projected continuous feasible region is contained in the other formulation's region, yielding no weaker finite infimal bound for any common minimization objective.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations represent the same integer solutions in the original-variable space \(\mathbb R^n\).
Their continuous relaxations are compared after projection to \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\subseteq P_2\) implies \(v_1(c)\ge v_2(c)\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) for which both infimal values are finite.

notation.meaning: projected continuous relaxation of formulation i
infimal relaxation value for objective vector c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projected-relaxation inclusion is the standard formulation-dominance order
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Representation Size
children.top_down_role: Variable, constraint, or auxiliary-structure burden of symmetry-breaking representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static size measures for symmetry-breaking formulations and extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear or mixed-integer formulation \(F\), define its structural size by \[s(F)=(n_a(F),m_a(F),\operatorname{nnz}_a(F)),\] where \(n_a(F)\) is the number of auxiliary variables, \(m_a(F)\) the number of added constraints, and \(\operatorname{nnz}_a(F)\) the number of added nonzero coefficients. When coefficient encoding matters, augment this tuple by the total binary encoding length \(L_a(F)\). Comparisons must use the same variable representation and counting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation size records added variables, constraints, nonzeros, and, when relevant, coefficient encoding length under a fixed counting convention.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is expressed in a fixed linear or mixed-integer representation.
Original-model and added formulation components are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(F)\), optionally augmented by \(L_a(F)\), measures the formulation’s added representation size.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variables, constraints, nonzeros, and encoding length are standard formulation-size measures

children.title: Strength-Size Tradeoff Frontier
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between relaxation quality and formulation footprint.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength-Size Tradeoff Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto frontier under relaxation dominance and componentwise representation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a family of symmetry-breaking formulations for the same integer set. Write \(F'\succeq F\) when the projected relaxation of \(F'\) is contained in that of \(F\), and write \(s(F')\le s(F)\) componentwise. A formulation \(F\in\mathcal F\) lies on the strength-size frontier if no \(F'\in\mathcal F\) satisfies both \(F'\succeq F\) and \(s(F')\le s(F)\), with at least one comparison strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation is frontier-efficient when no alternative is both at least as strong and no larger, with a strict improvement in one respect.
assumptions_latex: All formulations in \(\mathcal F\) encode the same integer solutions.
Strength and size use fixed common comparison conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Frontier formulations are precisely the nondominated elements under strength maximization and size minimization.

notation.meaning: F' has an equally strong or stronger projected relaxation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pareto nondominance formalizes the strength-size frontier

children.title: Numerical-Search Interaction Boundary
children.top_down_role: Numerical and search consequences of added representative restrictions.

children.title: Numerical Side Effects
children.top_down_role: Conditioning, scaling, tolerance, or degeneracy effects introduced by representative restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Side Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of numerical robustness despite unchanged exact symmetry coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive rescaling can leave a symmetry-breaking inequality unchanged in exact arithmetic while altering its numerical representation. Replacing \(a^\top x\le b\) by \(\alpha a^\top x\le\alpha b\), with \(\alpha>0\), preserves its feasible halfspace, but changes coefficient magnitudes and absolute residuals. In a larger constraint matrix, allowing \(\alpha\to 0\) or \(\alpha\to\infty\) can make coefficient ratios unbounded; consequently fixed feasibility tolerances, scaling rules, and floating-point linear algebra need not treat the equivalent formulations identically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly equivalent rescalings can create extreme coefficients and tolerance-dependent behavior, so logical symmetry coverage does not guarantee numerical equivalence.
assumptions_latex: Solver computations use finite precision and nonzero feasibility tolerances.
The inequality is embedded in a larger formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equivalence under positive scaling does not imply equivalent numerical behavior.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-precision behavior depends on scaling and tolerances

children.title: Search Side Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes to branching, propagation, node balance, or incumbent discovery caused by static restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Side Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of monotone branch-and-bound improvement from valid static constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_A(F)\) be the search tree generated by a fixed branch-and-bound implementation \(A\) on formulation \(F\). Even when valid symmetry-breaking constraints produce \(P_{F'}\subseteq P_F\) and preserve all integer optima up to symmetry, there is no general implication \(|T_A(F')|\le |T_A(F)|\). Added constraints may change presolve, branching scores, incumbent discovery, cut selection, node ordering, or degeneracy; hence the implementation may explore more nodes or consume more time on \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid, stronger symmetry breaking need not reduce a solver’s nodes or runtime because it can alter branching, presolve, cuts, and incumbent discovery.
assumptions_latex: \(F'\) adds valid symmetry-breaking constraints to \(F\).
\(A\) is an implementation whose decisions may depend on formulation data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation strengthening alone gives no monotone guarantee on \(|T_A(F)|\) or runtime.

notation.meaning: search tree produced by algorithm A on formulation F

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: branch-and-bound trajectories are formulation- and implementation-dependent

children.title: Numerical-Search Interactions
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical behavior alters the search consequences of symmetry-breaking formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Search Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling between numerical acceptance tests and discrete search decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(N\), let \(r_N\) denote computed constraint residuals and let \(\tau>0\) be the solver’s feasibility tolerance. Decisions based on the predicate \(r_N\le\tau\)—including incumbent acceptance, propagation, pruning, and cut activation—can change when scaling or floating-point error moves \(r_N\) across \(\tau\). Because each changed decision modifies descendant nodes and residuals, numerically equivalent symmetry-breaking formulations may induce different search trees even when their exact feasible sets coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small numerical differences can cross solver tolerances, change pruning or propagation, and thereby produce different downstream search trees.
assumptions_latex: Search decisions use computed residuals and finite tolerances.
The solver’s later state depends on earlier node decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numerical perturbations near \(\tau\) can propagate into discrete differences between search trees.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tolerance crossings couple finite-precision residuals to search decisions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Left-of ordering and solutions contained in a search node
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-tree conventions used in the correctness statement for isomorphism pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume branching on \(x_k\) creates a left child with \(x_k=1\) and a right child with \(x_k=0\). For distinct nodes \(N_a,N_b\), let \(N_d\) be their divergence ancestor. Node \(N_b\) is to the left of \(N_a\) if \(N_b\) descends from the left child of \(N_d\) and \(N_a\) descends from its right child. A vector \(\bar x\) is a solution in \(N_a\) if it is a feasible binary solution of the BIP and \[\bar x_i=1\quad(i\in F_a^1),\qquad \bar x_i=0\quad(i\in F_a^0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one-branches placed on the left and zero-branches on the right, one node is to the left of another when the nodes diverge in those respective directions at their common divergence ancestor. A solution in a node is a feasible binary solution satisfying all fixings defining that node.
assumptions_latex: \text{The left child fixes the branching variable to }1\text{ and the right child fixes it to }0
N_d\text{ is the ancestor at which }N_a\text{ and }N_b\text{ diverge}
\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\text{ is required for a solution of the BIP}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname{Sol}(N_a)\iff A\bar x\le b,\ \bar x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \bar x_i=1\ (i\in F_a^1),\ \bar x_i=0\ (i\in F_a^0)

source_evidence.locator: Enumeration / 9.3. Dealing with Symmetries / Definition 9.3-extra-4

knowledge_statements.title: Left-of ordering and solutions contained in a search node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of partial binary subproblems under a formulation symmetry; the extract also identifies repeated direct isomorphism comparison as computationally impractical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_a^0,F_a^1\) and \(F_b^0,F_b^1\) be the variable indices fixed to zero and one at nodes \(N_a,N_b\) of a variable-branching enumeration tree. The nodes are isomorphic if \[\exists\pi\in\Gamma:\quad \pi(F_b^1)=F_a^1\quad\text{and}\quad\pi(F_b^0)=F_a^0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two search nodes are isomorphic when a formulation symmetry maps both the zero-fixed and one-fixed index sets of one node to those of the other. The extract notes that checking every new node against existing nodes by direct isomorphism tests is too expensive for repeated use throughout the tree.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma\le\Sigma_n\text{ is the formulation symmetry group of the binary linear program}
F_a^0\cap F_a^1=\varnothing,\qquad F_b^0\cap F_b^1=\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_a\cong N_b\iff\exists\pi\in\Gamma:\ \pi(F_b^1)=F_a^1\ \land\ \pi(F_b^0)=F_a^0

source_evidence.locator: Enumeration / 9.3. Dealing with Symmetries / Definition 9.3-extra-2

knowledge_statements.title: Isomorphic nodes in variable-branching search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between the pruning rule, earlier isomorphic nodes, and preservation of every feasible-solution orbit represented by a pruned node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If node \(N_a\) has an isomorphic node to its left in the enumeration tree, then \(N_a\) is pruned by the isomorphism rule. Conversely, if \(N_a\) is pruned by that rule, then for every solution \(\bar x\) in \(N_a\), there exist a node \(N_b\) to the left of \(N_a\) and a solution \(\bar y\) in \(N_b\) that is isomorphic to \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isomorphic node already lying to the left causes the current node to be pruned. Conversely, every solution in a node pruned by the rule has an isomorphic solution in some node to its left, so pruning does not eliminate the represented solution orbit.
assumptions_latex: \text{Variable branching creates the }x_k=1\text{ child on the left and the }x_k=0\text{ child on the right}
\text{Node isomorphism and the pruning rule are defined using the formulation symmetry group }\Gamma
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\exists N_b\text{ left of }N_a:\ N_b\cong N_a\right)\Rightarrow\operatorname{prune}(N_a),\qquad \operatorname{prune}(N_a)\Rightarrow\forall\bar x\in\operatorname{Sol}(N_a)\ \exists N_b\text{ left of }N_a\ \exists\bar y\in\operatorname{Sol}(N_b):\bar y\cong\bar x

children.title: Canonical Node Tests
children.top_down_role: Canonicality tests for partial search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Node Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic canonicality test for partial assignments under residual symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a search node represented by a partial assignment \(p\), a group \(G\) acting on such assignments, and a total order \(\preceq\) invariantly defined on their encodings. Compute \(p^{\star}=\min_{\preceq}\{g p:g\in G\}\). Retain the node exactly when \(p=p^{\star}\); otherwise prune it as isomorphic to the canonical node \(p^{\star}\). Stop after finding any image strictly preceding \(p\), or after certifying that none exists. The output is respectively “prune” or “canonical.”
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare a partial search state with all symmetry images; retain it only if it is the least image under the prescribed order.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) preserves the node subproblem represented by each orbit.
\(\preceq\) is a total order on node encodings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicality test for a partial search state using the ordered variable-branching path and the formulation symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N_a\), let \(p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\) be the ordered variable indices branched on along the path from the root to \(N_a\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node when a formulation symmetry preserves the required earlier one-fixings along the branching path and maps a later path variable fixed to zero into the node's one-fixed set.

children.title: Stabilizer-Chain Pruning
children.top_down_role: Pruning organized through residual stabilizer information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilizer-Chain Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental canonical pruning using stabilizers of fixed branching decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetry group \(G\), an ordered base \((b_1,\ldots,b_k)\), and a partial assignment \(p\). Form the chain \(G=G^{(0)}\ge G^{(1)}\ge\cdots\ge G^{(k)}\), where \(G^{(i)}\) fixes \(b_1,ldots,b_i\). At each branching level, intersect the current group with the stabilizer of all decisions already fixed by \(p\). Use the resulting residual-group orbits and transversal representatives to search for an image of \(p\) preceding it canonically. Prune upon finding such an image; otherwise retain the node and pass its residual stabilizer to its children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain stabilizers of earlier decisions and use their orbits to detect a canonically earlier equivalent node, pruning when one exists.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) preserves the original optimization problem.
The base and transversals represent the required stabilizer chain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A node is pruned when residual stabilizer information certifies a canonically earlier equivalent node.

notation.meaning: pointwise stabilizer of the first i base points

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stabilizer chains support incremental orbit and canonicality computation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record conflates a base-point stabilizer chain with stabilizers of branching decisions and does not specify why the residual-group search certifies canonicality relative to the full node orbit. The text also contains the typo `b_1,ldots,b_i`. An authoritative source for the exact pruning variant is required before its hypotheses or algorithm can be corrected reliably.

children.title: Canonical Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Search generation restricted to canonical extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isomorph-free generation through an equivariant parent map and canonical representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be a graded family with group action, let \(\pi\) delete one augmentation, and let \(c(y)\) be a fixed canonical representative of the orbit of \(y\). Initialize with the canonical root. From a retained canonical object \(x\), enumerate candidate children \(y\) with \(\pi(y)=x\), taking one representative from each stabilizer orbit of augmentations. Retain \(y\) only when \(\pi(c(y))=x\); otherwise reject it. Continue until the target grade, outputting the retained canonical objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate only extensions whose canonical representative deletes back to the current canonical parent, using one extension per stabilizer orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is compatible with the group action.
\(c\) selects one fixed representative of every orbit.
Children are exhaustively generated modulo the parent stabilizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted augmentation rule generates canonical representatives without retaining isomorphic duplicates.

notation.meaning: canonical representative of the orbit of y

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical construction paths use compatible parent and canonical-label tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Equivariance of the parent map and an arbitrary canonical representative map do not ensure the literal equality \(\pi(c(y))=x\). The stated test can therefore reject valid orbit representatives, and calling retained children canonical is not justified. The exact canonical-construction-path theorem and compatibility conditions require a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Orbital Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-way branching on an orbit of unfixed binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(N\), let \(G_N\) preserve the node subproblem and let \(O\) be the \(G_N\)-orbit of an unfixed binary variable index \(i\). Create two children: \[x_i=1,\qquad\text{or}\qquad x_j=0\ \text{for every }j\in O.\] Any binary assignment has either no unit entry in \(O\), placing it in the second branch, or a unit entry that a symmetry in \(G_N\) can map to index \(i\), placing an equivalent assignment in the first branch. Update the residual group separately in each child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary-variable orbit, branch on one chosen variable being one versus every variable in the orbit being zero.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(j\in O\).
\(G_N\) preserves the current node subproblem and acts transitively on \(O\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two branches cover every residual symmetry class represented at node \(N\).

notation.meaning: residual symmetry group at node N
orbit of the selected binary-variable index

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Orbital Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured orbital branching for binary variables arranged in interchangeable matrix blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node let \(G\) preserve the node subproblem, and let \(O=Gx_{rc}\) be the orbit of an unfixed binary matrix entry \(x_{rc}\). Create the disjoint children \[x_{rc}=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad \sum_{x_{ij}\in O}x_{ij}=0.\] In the first child, retain only one symmetry-equivalent representative among choices of an orbit member set to one, using the matrix block's prescribed row or column order; in the second, fix every entry in \(O\) to zero. Update the residual symmetry group after either child is formed. The two children preserve at least one representative of every parent-node solution orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on one matrix entry being one versus its entire residual orbit being zero, then retain canonical representatives and update the residual symmetry group.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) for every entry in the selected block.
\(G\) acts by variable permutations and preserves the node subproblem.
The representative order is fixed within the selected structured block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children preserve at least one representative of every feasible-solution orbit of the parent node.

notation.meaning: residual symmetry group at the current node
orbit of the selected matrix entry under the residual group

children.title: Orbit Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for choosing a variable orbit or object orbit at a search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local selection of a branching orbit from the residual group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node subproblem, its residual symmetry group \(G\), and the set \(U\) of unfixed binary variables, form the non-singleton candidate orbits \(\mathcal O=\{Gx_i:x_i\in U,\ |Gx_i|>1\}\). Assign each \(O\in\mathcal O\) a deterministic score \(s(O)\), which may combine orbit size, relaxation fractionality, and estimated balance of the disjunction. Select \[O^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{O\in\mathcal O}s(O),\] resolving ties by a fixed variable order. If \(\mathcal O\) is empty, orbital branching is inapplicable at that node; otherwise branch using \(O^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score all nontrivial residual orbits, choose a highest-scoring orbit with deterministic tie-breaking, and use ordinary branching when no such orbit exists.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) preserves the current node subproblem.
\(s(O)\) is computable from node-local information.
Ties are resolved by a fixed total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy returns one eligible orbit or declares that orbital branching is unavailable.

notation.meaning: unfixed binary variables at the node

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for this leaf, but the scoring family is presented as a general orbit-selection policy without evidence that these criteria form a recognized policy. The plain statement also prescribes ordinary branching when no orbit exists, whereas the mathematical statement only declares orbital branching inapplicable. A specific source is needed to determine the intended policy and fallback.

children.title: Residual-Group Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Node-local tracking of symmetries compatible with prior branching decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Group Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental restriction of node symmetries after branching and propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the root residual group as \(G_{ho}=G_0\). For a child node \(v\) of node \(u\), let \(D_v\) denote all accumulated bounds, fixings, and branching constraints. Update \[G_v=\{g\in G_u:g(D_v)=D_v\}.\] Equivalently, intersect \(G_u\) with the setwise stabilizers of newly introduced bound classes and branching sets, using pointwise stabilizers when individual variable-value assignments must remain fixed. Store generators for \(G_v\) and compute subsequent variable orbits only under \(G_v\). An element removed at an ancestor is never reintroduced below that ancestor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain at each node the subgroup preserving every accumulated decision, and compute later orbits only from generators of that subgroup.
assumptions_latex: \(G_0\) preserves the root optimization model.
Every node decision has a defined image under the variable action.
Group generators and stabilizers can be computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(g\in G_v\) preserves the complete node subproblem at \(v\).

notation.meaning: accumulated decisions defining child node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Residual-Group Maintenance and the subgroup formula is plausible, but no source supports the precise setwise-versus-pointwise update rule or the generator-maintenance prescription. A specialized group-theoretic branching reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Orbit-Group Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of available orbit choices on the current residual symmetry group.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Group Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency requirement linking an orbital branch with its child residual groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_u\) preserve node \(u\), and let an orbital disjunction be constructed from an orbit \(O=G_ux_i\). For each child \(v\), compute \(G_v\) as the subgroup of \(G_u\) preserving that child's entire defining constraint set. All orbit fixing, orbit scoring, and later orbital branching at \(v\) must use orbits of \(G_v\), not orbits inherited unchanged from \(G_u\). Consequently, an orbit may split after branching but cannot merge variables belonging to distinct \(G_u\)-orbits. This coupling makes every subsequent symmetry reduction valid for the actual child subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each orbital branch must induce child-specific residual groups; subsequent reductions use their refined orbits, which may split but cannot merge parent orbits.
assumptions_latex: \(G_v\leq G_u\) preserves every constraint defining child \(v\).
The parent branching orbit is computed under \(G_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every child orbit is contained in a parent orbit, and node-local reductions remain symmetry-valid.

notation.meaning: parent and child residual symmetry groups

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the Orbit-Group Coupling leaf, and subgroup orbits do refine parent-group orbits. However, the stronger claim that the stated coupling suffices to validate every later reduction depends on the exact residual-group construction and reduction rules, neither of which is cited.

children.title: Binary Orbital Fixing
children.top_down_role: Classical orbital propagation for binary domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Orbital Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-preserving zero fixings induced by ordered binary branching decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(i_1,\ldots,i_k\) be the ordered binary variables selected as one-branches on the root-to-node path. For each \(t\), let \(H_{t-1}\) be the subgroup preserving the node decisions preceding \(x_{i_t}=1\), and let \(O_t=H_{t-1}i_t\). Retain the canonical alternative \(x_{i_t}=1\) and impose \(x_j=0\) for every eligible \(j\in O_t\setminus\{i_t\}\) not distinguished by an earlier decision. Apply the fixings cumulatively. The reduced node need not contain every feasible solution, but it contains a representative of every solution orbit compatible with the path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a canonical one-branch, fix symmetry-equivalent eligible binary variables to zero while preserving one representative of every compatible solution orbit.
assumptions_latex: All affected variables are binary.
Each \(H_{t-1}\) preserves the subproblem defined before decision \(t\).
The path uses a fixed canonical ordering convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cumulative fixings preserve at least one representative of every compatible feasible-solution orbit.

notation.meaning: residual subgroup before the t-th one-decision
orbit of the selected variable at decision t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed one-branch fixing rule is false in general. After setting one member of an orbit to one, fixing every other eligible orbit member to zero can remove all representatives of feasible orbits containing multiple ones; symmetric binary models with a requirement such as a cardinality of at least two give immediate counterexamples. Classical orbital fixing instead requires a precisely defined fixing history and stabilizer rule. This record cannot be repaired without replacing its mathematical content.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local zero fixing using orbits under the stabilizer of the indices already fixed to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N_a\) be a node of the enumeration tree, and let \(\mathcal O_a\) be the family of orbits of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) under \(\operatorname{stabil}(F_a^1,\Gamma)\). Define
\[
Z=\bigcup\left\{O\in\mathcal O_a: O\cap F_a^0\neq\varnothing\ \text{and}\ O\setminus F_a^0\neq\varnothing\right\}.
\]
If \(Z\neq\varnothing\), create a child \(N_{a'}\) of \(N_a\) and set \(F_{a'}^0:=F_a^0\cup Z\). The variables indexed by \(Z\setminus F_a^0\) are thereby fixed to zero by orbital fixing at \(N_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an enumeration-tree node, collect every residual-symmetry orbit containing both an index already fixed to zero and an index not fixed to zero. If their union is nonempty, create a child and add the entire union to its zero-fixed set; the newly added indices are fixed to zero by orbital fixing.
assumptions_latex: N_a\text{ is a node of the enumeration tree.}
\mathcal O_a\text{ is the orbit family of }\{1,\ldots,n\}\text{ under }\operatorname{stabil}(F_a^1,\Gamma).
Z=\bigcup\{O\in\mathcal O_a:O\cap F_a^0\neq\varnothing,\ O\setminus F_a^0\neq\varnothing\}.
Z\neq\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists N_{a'}\text{ child of }N_a\text{ with }F_{a'}^0=F_a^0\cup Z,\text{ so every index in }Z\setminus F_a^0\text{ is newly fixed to zero.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correctness Basis for Binary Orbital Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an earlier isomorphic solution when a current solution activates an orbit already intersecting the zero-fixed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_a\) be a node of the enumeration tree and let \(\bar x\) be a solution in \(N_a\). If there exist \(O\in\mathcal O_a\) and \(i\in O\) such that \(O\cap F_a^0\neq\varnothing\) and \(\bar x_i=1\), then there exists a node \(N_b\) to the left of \(N_a\) that contains a solution isomorphic to \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a solution at the current node assigns value one to an index in an orbit that also contains an index already fixed to zero, then an isomorphic solution occurs in a node to the left of the current node.
assumptions_latex: N_a\text{ is a node of the enumeration tree.}
\bar x\text{ is a solution in }N_a.
\exists O\in\mathcal O_a:\ O\cap F_a^0\neq\varnothing.
\exists i\in O:\ \bar x_i=1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists N_b\text{ to the left of }N_a\text{ containing a solution isomorphic to }\bar x.

assumptions_latex: Every variable domain \(D_i\) is finite.
\(G\) preserves node feasibility and acts compatibly on variables and values.
\(\preceq\) is a fixed total order on assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected domains retain at least one representative of every feasible \(G\)-orbit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical domain pruning for finite-domain variables under residual symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node let \(G\) preserve the subproblem and permute variables whose finite domains and value semantics are compatible. Let \(F\) be the set of domain-feasible assignments and fix a total order \(\preceq\) on assignments. Define the retained representatives by \[F^{\mathrm{can}}=\{x\in F:x\preceq gx\text{ for every }g\in G\}.\] For each variable \(i\), replace its domain by the projection \(D_i'=\{x_i:x\in F^{\mathrm{can}}\}\); iterate after every bound or domain change. If \(F^{\mathrm{can}}\) is empty, prune the node. Otherwise the reduced domains retain at least one assignment from each \(G\)-orbit in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict finite domains to values appearing in canonical representatives of residual-group assignment orbits, pruning the node only when none remains.

children.title: Stabilizer Selection for Orbital Reduction
children.top_down_role: Residual-subgroup choices compatible with accumulated decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilizer Selection for Orbital Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for residual subgroups used in node-local orbital reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_u\) be the complete set of constraints, bounds, domain restrictions, and canonical decisions accumulated at node \(u\), and let \(G_0\) be a symmetry group of the root model. A subgroup \(H_u\leq G_0\) is admissible for orbital reduction at \(u\) precisely when \[h(D_u)=D_u\quad\text{for every }h\in H_u.\] Setwise stabilization is sufficient for interchangeable collections of identical decisions; pointwise stabilization is required when the identity of a fixed variable or ordered decision is significant. Orbital reductions at \(u\) may use any admissible \(H_u\), with larger admissible subgroups generally producing coarser orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use only subgroups preserving the entire node description, choosing setwise or pointwise stabilizers according to whether individual decision identities matter.
assumptions_latex: \(G_0\) preserves the root model.
\(D_u\) includes every accumulated node restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every orbit computed under an admissible \(H_u\) consists of variables interchangeable within the node subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is the correct content kind for this leaf. The admissibility criterion is plausible, but the precise necessity claim and the distinction between setwise and pointwise stabilization depend on how canonical and ordered decisions are encoded. No inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary propagation for a fixed row and column ordering of an orbitope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\{0,1\}^{p\times q}\) have column-permutation symmetry, and fix the representative convention \(X_{\bullet 1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\bullet q}\) using the original row order. Given node fixings, let \(C\) be the binary completions satisfying both those fixings and the lexicographic column order. If \(C=\varnothing\), prune the node. Otherwise fix \(x_{ij}=b\) whenever \(x_{ij}=b\) for every \(X\in C\), and leave it unfixed when both values occur in \(C\). Thus the procedure computes all coordinate fixings implied by the static orbitope and the current node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under fixed matrix orders, prune if no lex-sorted completion exists and fix exactly those entries constant across all such completions.

children.title: Dynamic Orbitopal Fixing

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Orbitopal Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary orbitopal propagation using a search-dependent row order fixed along each branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\{0,1\}^{p\times q}\) have column-permutation symmetry. At node \(u\), construct a row order \(\pi_u\) from the branching history, extending the ancestor order without changing earlier comparisons, and require \(X_{\bullet1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex},\pi_u}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex},\pi_u}X_{\bullet q}\). Let \(C_u\) be the completions satisfying this order and all node fixings. Prune when \(C_u=\varnothing\); otherwise fix \(x_{ij}=b\) exactly when every matrix in \(C_u\) has that value. Descendants may append new comparison rows but must preserve the order already used at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a branch-dependent row order, then derive every binary fixing common to all node completions whose columns are lexicographically sorted in that order.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is binary and its columns are interchangeable.
\(\pi_u\) is compatible with all ancestor comparison choices.
Node restrictions preserve the selected column symmetry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dynamic propagation preserves one representative per compatible column orbit and derives all coordinate consequences for \(C_u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and binary dynamic-orbitopal scope fit the leaf. No source establishes that the stated ancestor-compatible row-order extension is the intended dynamic convention or that it yields all coordinate consequences while preserving one representative per compatible orbit.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Suborbitope Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact propagation inside the node-local face induced by accumulated matrix fixings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary matrix \(X\) with interchangeable columns, let \(F_u\) be the face determined by all fixings at node \(u\). Partition the still-interchangeable columns into maximal blocks on which the residual column group acts as a full symmetric group. For each block, impose the inherited lexicographic column order and let \(S_u\) be the set of matrices in \(F_u\) satisfying all block orders. Prune if \(S_u=\varnothing\); otherwise fix \(x_{ij}=b\) whenever that equality holds for every \(X\in S_u\). Recompute the blocks and repeat until no additional fixing is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identify maximal fully symmetric column blocks on the node face and iteratively fix entries constant across every lex-ordered completion of those blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is binary.
The residual action on every selected block is the full symmetric group.
Inherited block orders are compatible with ancestor decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, every coordinate constant on the node-local full suborbitope is fixed.

notation.meaning: node face induced by accumulated fixings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the terminal container, but the record does not cite a definition of a full suborbitope or justify the maximal-block construction. Full symmetric projections on individual blocks do not by themselves establish that the residual action decomposes independently across those blocks, so the simultaneous ordering and exact-fixing claims require a specialized source.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Domain Orbitopal Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic matrix-domain propagation for interchangeable columns with finite nonbinary entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) have entries in finite totally ordered domains and interchangeable columns. At node \(u\), choose an ancestor-compatible row order \(\pi_u\) and define \(C_u\) as the domain-feasible completions satisfying \(X_{\bullet1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex},\pi_u}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex},\pi_u}X_{\bullet q}\). If \(C_u=\varnothing\), prune the node. Otherwise replace each entry domain by \[D'_{ij}=\{X_{ij}:X\in C_u\}.\] Recompute these projections after every domain change until a fixed point is reached. The remaining domains retain at least one lexicographic representative of every compatible column-permutation orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite nonbinary matrices, project all dynamically lex-sorted completions onto each entry and iterate the resulting domain reductions to a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: Every entry domain is finite and totally ordered.
The columns are interchangeable under the node subproblem.
The dynamic row order is compatible with ancestor decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-point domains retain at least one representative of every compatible column orbit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the general-domain orbitopal leaf, but no source supports this finite-domain extension, its ancestor-compatible dynamic ordering, or the asserted fixed-point propagation strength. These details cannot be validated from the unrelated local source inventory.

children.title: Static Lexicographic Fixing
children.top_down_role: Propagation under fixed lexicographic representative orders.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Lexicographic Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact domain propagation under fixed lex-leader inequalities for a permutation group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\prod_{i=1}^nD_i\) be a finite product of totally ordered domains, let \(G\) permute coordinates while preserving feasibility, and fix the coordinate order \(1,\ldots,n\). Define the static lex-leader set \[L=\{x\in D:x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}gx\text{ for every }g\in G\}.\] At a search node, let \(C\subseteq L\) contain the lex leaders compatible with all current domains and constraints. Prune if \(C=\varnothing\); otherwise replace each domain by \(D_i'=\{x_i:x\in C\}\). Iterate to a fixed point without changing the coordinate order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed coordinate order, project all compatible lex leaders onto each variable domain and iterate; prune when no lex leader remains.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i\) is finite and totally ordered.
\(G\) acts by feasibility-preserving coordinate permutations.
The lexicographic coordinate order is fixed globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced domains contain exactly the coordinate values supported by compatible static lex leaders.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and fixed-order scope fit Static Lexicographic Fixing, and the projection statement is internally coherent. Nevertheless, no citation with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator supports this exact lex-leader propagation formulation, so candidate-review acceptance is not available.

children.title: Dynamic Permutation Reduction
children.top_down_role: Search-dependent lexicographic reduction for permutation actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Permutation Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-dependent lexicographic reduction under coordinate permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(u\), let \(D_u\subseteq X\) be its current domain and let \(G_u\leq G\) preserve \(D_u\) and the objective. Fix a coordinate order and retain only completions satisfying \[x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}} g(x)\qquad(g\in G_u).\] Domain propagation may delete a value only when every completion using that value violates one of these inequalities. Recompute \(G_u\) and the induced reductions after branching; output the reduced domain when no further deletion is possible. Every \(G_u\)-orbit intersecting \(D_u\) then retains a lexicographically maximal representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, retain lexicographically maximal representatives under the permutations preserving that node, and propagate only deletions incompatible with every such representative.
assumptions_latex: \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for all \(g\in G_u\) and \(x\in D_u\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_u/G_u\) retains at least one representative of every feasible local orbit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source supports the node-dependent stabilizer recomputation or propagation claim. Moreover, \(D_u/G_u\) denotes an orbit space rather than a domain that retains representatives.

children.title: Dynamic Signed-Permutation Reduction
children.top_down_role: Search-dependent lexicographic reduction for signed and reflection actions.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Detecting and Handling Reflection Symmetries in Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming and Beyond — Hojny

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Signed-Permutation Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-dependent lexicographic reduction under signed coordinate actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(u\), transform bounded variables to centered coordinates \(y=x-c\). Let \(H_u\) be a group of signed permutation matrices satisfying \(c+h(y)\in D_u\) whenever \(c+y\in D_u\), and preserving the objective. Retain completions for which \[y\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}h(y)\qquad(h\in H_u).\] Delete a domain value only if no completion containing it satisfies all inequalities. After every branch, recompute the admissible stabilizer \(H_u\); terminate at propagation closure. Each local signed orbit retains a lexicographically maximal completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Center the variables, compute the signed symmetries valid at the node, and retain a lexicographically maximal completion from every local signed orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(D_u\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is invariant under \(y\mapsto h(y)\) about \(c\)
\(f(c+h(y))=f(c+y)\) for every \(h\in H_u\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible \(H_u\)-orbit has a retained representative.

notation.meaning: Valid signed-permutation group at node u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the centered signed action, admissible stabilizer, and completeness of the stated reductions require a specialized source. The relationship between the action on \(y\) and invariance of the original domain in \(x\) also needs precise support.

children.title: Explicit Subsymmetry Formulations
children.top_down_role: Model-based encodings that activate representative restrictions in prescribed regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Subsymmetry Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional formulations encoding canonical representatives in prescribed regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the feasible set and let regions \(R_k\) have symmetry groups \(G_k\) preserving \(X\cap R_k\) and the objective. Introduce binary indicators \(z_k\) with a valid formulation of \(z_k=1\Longleftrightarrow x\in R_k\). For each \(k\), impose \[z_k=1\Longrightarrow x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}g(x)\quad(g\in G_k).\] Any linearization must be exact on integer-feasible points. The resulting formulation represents the original feasible orbits while selecting a canonical representative whenever a prescribed region is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Region indicators activate lexicographic representative constraints for the subgroup valid in each region, without changing the represented feasible orbits.
assumptions_latex: \(G_k(X\cap R_k)=X\cap R_k\)
\(f(gx)=f(x)\) on \(X\cap R_k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation preserves feasibility modulo symmetry and enforces local canonicality in every active region.

notation.meaning: Symmetry group valid within the region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the container, but independent regional canonicality constraints need not automatically have a common representative when regions overlap or different local groups interact. A source or additional compatibility hypotheses are required for the orbit-preservation conclusion.

children.title: Activation Handlers
children.top_down_role: Solver mechanisms for detecting active local symmetries and enabling compatible handling methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation Handlers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search handlers that certify and activate local symmetry methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given certified pairs \((A_k,M_k)\), where predicate \(A_k(u)\) implies that method \(M_k\) is valid for every completion below node \(u\), evaluate the predicates after node-domain changes. Activate \(M_k\) whenever \(A_k(u)\) becomes true, apply its propagation or separation to closure, and store the activation on the node. On backtracking, discard activations whose predicates are no longer certified. The handler outputs the locally reduced node domain and must never activate a method solely from an unverified heuristic match.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect certified local-symmetry conditions, activate their compatible methods to closure, and revoke node-specific activations upon backtracking.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k(u)\Rightarrow M_k\) preserves one feasible representative per active local orbit
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every handler-induced reduction is valid for all completions below \(u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for this solver-mechanism leaf, but the activation, closure, storage, and backtracking semantics are uncited and implementation-dependent. The certification condition must be supported by a precise solver or subsymmetry reference.

children.title: Local Symmetry-Handling Method Family
children.top_down_role: Specialized dynamic methods for locally active matrix or group structures.

children.title: Local Orbitope Methods
children.top_down_role: Dynamic handling specialized to locally active matrix structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Orbitope Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbitopal reduction for locally interchangeable binary-matrix columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(u\), identify a binary submatrix \(Y\in\{0,1\}^{p\times q}\) whose feasible completions are invariant under every column permutation in \(S_q\). Order its columns lexicographically and impose \[Y_{\ast 1}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}Y_{\ast 2}\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}Y_{\ast q}.\] Apply orbitopal fixing by deleting precisely those local variable values that occur in no completion satisfying this order. Output the resulting node domain; validity is restricted to the subtree in which the certified interchangeability remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When binary-matrix columns are locally interchangeable, sort them lexicographically and remove values absent from every ordered completion.
assumptions_latex: \(S_q\) preserves all feasible completions below \(u\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least one representative of each local column-permutation orbit remains.

notation.meaning: Column j of the local binary submatrix
Full permutation group on q columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the local-orbitope container and its representative claim is plausible under full column interchangeability, but the exact fixing variant and subtree-validity conditions lack an inspectable specialized citation.

children.title: Local-Group Methods
children.top_down_role: Dynamic handling based on groups active within restricted search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Group Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic orbit reduction under a certified node-local subgroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(u\), compute a subgroup \(G_u\) that preserves the objective and all feasible completions compatible with the node domain. Choose a canonicalization or orbit-propagation routine valid for the action of \(G_u\), apply it until no further domain reduction occurs, and attach the resulting state only to the subtree rooted at \(u\). A deletion is permitted only if another member of the same \(G_u\)-orbit remains attainable or if the deleted value cannot belong to any chosen canonical representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a certified symmetry subgroup valid below the current node to canonicalize or propagate local orbits without losing an orbit representative.
assumptions_latex: \(G_u(D_u\cap X)=D_u\cap X\)
\(f(gx)=f(x)\) for \(g\in G_u\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced subtree retains an objective-equivalent representative of every original local orbit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic local-group scope fits, but no particular canonicalization or propagation algorithm is specified. Merely requiring another orbit member to remain attainable at each deletion does not by itself establish that a sequence of deletions preserves a representative; an invariant and source are needed.

children.title: Local Structure Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice between matrix-specific handling and broader local group machinery.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Structure Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-first selection among certified local symmetry structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{C}_u\) be the finite set of symmetry structures certified at node \(u\). A selector may assign a method \(M(C)\) to each chosen \(C\in\mathcal{C}_u\) only when its validity conditions hold on the entire corresponding subtree. Simultaneously selected methods must have disjoint supports or a certificate that their reductions are jointly representative-preserving. Among compatible assignments, a score based on expected reduction minus computational cost may be optimized; uncertified structures receive no method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose methods only for certified local structures, require compatibility among overlapping reductions, and optimize effectiveness only after validity is established.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{C}_u\) contains only subtree-valid certificates
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected method family jointly preserves at least one feasible representative of every relevant orbit.

notation.meaning: Certified local structures at node u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the selection leaf, but the claimed sufficiency of disjoint supports and the form of a joint representative-preservation certificate require a formal reference. The scoring rule is also an uncited design prescription.

children.title: Independent Factor Detection
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of detected symmetry into independently handled components.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Factor Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-product detection from disjoint generator supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\langle S\rangle\) act on variable indices and partition the generators as \(S=S_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_r\). If the moved-index supports \(V_i=\bigcup_{g\in S_i}\operatorname{supp}(g)\) are pairwise disjoint, then the subgroups \(G_i=\langle S_i\rangle\) commute, intersect trivially, and satisfy \[G=G_1\times\cdots\times G_r.\] Consequently, representative-preserving symmetry methods can be applied independently factor by factor, provided each method acts only on its corresponding support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generators with pairwise disjoint moved-variable supports yield commuting direct-product factors that can be handled independently.
assumptions_latex: \(V_i\cap V_j=\varnothing\) whenever \(i\ne j\)
\(G=\langle S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_r\rangle\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\cong\prod_{i=1}^r G_i\), with independent actions on the supports \(V_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct-product statement for permutation subgroups with pairwise disjoint moved supports is mathematically standard and the property kind fits. Nevertheless, the record supplies no citation, and the solver-level conclusion about independently composing representative-preserving methods needs explicit support.

children.title: Embedded Symmetry Recognition Family
children.top_down_role: Identification of specialized structures inside a larger group.

children.title: Hidden Orbitope Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition of latent orbitope structure within a broader detected action.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Orbitope Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of an embedded full column-permutation action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given permutation generators on model variables, enumerate candidate arrays \(Y=(y_{ij})\) of binary variables with common row and column dimensions. Accept \(Y\) as a hidden orbitope only if the induced generator restrictions fix row indices and generate the full column action \(S_q\), while every generator maps constraints, bounds, integrality, and objective coefficients invariantly. Return the array, its induced column group, and the certificate mapping each generator action to a column permutation; otherwise return no recognition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover a binary array whose certified symmetry generators induce the full permutation group on its columns, and return the action certificate.
assumptions_latex: The supplied generators are certified model automorphisms
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted array supports valid column-orbitope symmetry handling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the recognition leaf, but candidate-array enumeration, verification of a full induced column action, and the sufficiency of the returned certificate are not sourced or specified sufficiently to assess reliability.

children.title: Hidden Subgroup Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition of useful subgroups embedded within a larger symmetry group.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Subgroup Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction and certification of an embedded structured subgroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a certified model-automorphism group \(G=\langle S\rangle\) and a candidate variable set \(V\), compute the setwise stabilizer \(H=\{g\in G:g(V)=V\}\) and its induced action on \(V\). Match this action against a prescribed structured-group representation only through an explicit bijection of moved variables and generators. Verify that the matched generators preserve all relevant constraints, domains, and objective coefficients. Return \(H\), the representation map, and verification data; reject the match if any check fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extract a stabilizer on selected variables, match its induced action to a structured subgroup, and accept only with an explicit model-invariance certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a certified model-automorphism group
\(V\) is a finite variable-index set
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(H\) is a certified symmetry subgroup on \(V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the hidden-subgroup recognition container, but the prescribed representation family, matching procedure, and verification data are unspecified. A specialized source is needed to establish the claimed recognition algorithm and certificate.

children.title: Recognition Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Cases where the available representation does not identify a unique specialized structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Recognition Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness and unsoundness boundaries for inferred symmetry structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generator action need not determine a unique embedded structure. For example, the natural action of \(S_4\) on four interchangeable variables can be represented as permutation of four scalar positions or as permutation of four columns of a one-row binary array. These recognitions prescribe different specialized handlers despite encoding the same abstract action. Therefore group isomorphism or matching orbit sizes alone cannot certify a structure; variable incidence, domains, constraints, and the explicit action map must also be verified. Applying a handler from an uncertified interpretation may remove valid representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same permutation action can admit multiple structural interpretations, so orbit sizes or abstract group matches alone cannot justify a specialized symmetry handler.
assumptions_latex: \(S_4\) acts naturally on four interchangeable variables
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structural recognition is nonunique, and uncertified handler selection is not validity-preserving in general.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind, and structural nonuniqueness is plausible. However, the one-row-array example does not by itself demonstrate that the interpretations lead to materially different or unsound handlers, so the concrete failure claim needs a source or a better certified counterexample.

children.title: Componentwise Method Selection
children.top_down_role: Assignment of static, orbital, orbitopal, lexicographic, or inequality-based methods by component.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Method Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment of symmetry methods to independent detected factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the detected symmetry group decomposes as \(G=G_1\times\cdots\times G_r\) on pairwise disjoint supports. For each factor \(G_i\), select at most one primary method from static fixing, orbital branching, orbitopal fixing, lexicographic reduction, or symmetry-breaking inequalities, and verify that its hypotheses hold for the induced action. Methods assigned to distinct supports may be composed. If supports overlap, composition requires a separate certificate that the combined restrictions retain a representative of every \(G\)-orbit; otherwise the conflicting assignments must not be used together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign a valid symmetry method separately to each independent factor; overlapping methods require an additional certificate that their combined reductions preserve representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(G=\prod_{i=1}^r G_i\) with pairwise disjoint supports
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified componentwise assignments jointly preserve an objective-equivalent representative of every \(G\)-orbit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits componentwise selection, but no source supports the one-primary-method rule or the assertion that methods on distinct supports may always be composed. Method-specific state, branching, and canonical restrictions may require stronger compatibility hypotheses.

children.top_down_role: Compatibility of representative conventions imposed by multiple symmetry-handling methods.

children.title: Independent-Support Composition
children.top_down_role: Composition of methods acting on independent supports or group factors.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is invariant under \(G=G_1\times G_2\), and the factors act on disjoint coordinate supports.
For \(i=1,2\), \(R_i\subseteq X\) contains exactly one representative of every \(G_i\)-orbit and is invariant under the other factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\cap R_2\) contains exactly one representative of every \(G\)-orbit in \(X\).

notation.meaning: Representative sets imposed by the two methods

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-group composition for exact representative restrictions on disjoint coordinate supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be invariant under \(G=G_1\times G_2\), where \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) act on disjoint coordinate supports and hence commute. Suppose \(R_i\subseteq X\) intersects every \(G_i\)-orbit in exactly one point and is invariant under \(G_{3-i}\), for \(i\in\{1,2\}\). Then each \(G\)-orbit intersects \(R_1\cap R_2\) in exactly one point. Thus the two representative-selection methods may be imposed simultaneously without deleting an orbit or retaining two representatives from one orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact representative restrictions for commuting symmetry factors on disjoint supports compose by intersection, provided each restriction is invariant under the other factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Support Composition

children.title: Shared Dynamic Ordering
children.top_down_role: Composition of dynamic methods coordinated by a common search-dependent order.

assumptions_latex: At search node \(v\), every participating method uses the same strict total order \(\prec_v\) on the active symmetric objects.
The rule producing \(\prec_v\) from the search history is equivariant under every symmetry retained at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All participating methods select representatives according to one search-dependent canonical convention at \(v\).

notation.meaning: Shared strict total order at the node
Symmetry group retained at the node

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for dynamic symmetry methods driven by search-dependent object orderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(v\), let \(G_v\) be the retained symmetry group and let \(\prec_v\) be a strict total order on the active symmetric objects. Dynamic symmetry methods are consistently coordinated when they all use \(\prec_v\), and the history-to-order map is equivariant: for every \(g\in G_v\), transforming the node history by \(g\) transforms \(\prec_v\) by the same action. Under this condition, orbit comparisons, branching priorities, and representative tests made by the participating methods use one common canonical convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic symmetry methods are compatible when they share one node-specific total order whose construction transforms equivariantly with the retained symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Dynamic Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-order and equivariance conditions are clear, but no inspectable source establishes that they suffice for the stated canonical coordination of orbit comparisons, branching priorities, and representative tests.

children.title: Overlapping Representative Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Incompatibilities caused by overlapping methods using different representative conventions.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\{(0,1),(1,0)\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^2\), with symmetry group generated by swapping the two coordinates.
Two methods impose opposite representative conventions on the same coordinate orbit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\cap\{x_1\ge x_2\}\cap\{x_1\le x_2\}=\varnothing\), although \(X\ne\varnothing\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal binary example showing orbit loss from incompatible conventions on overlapping support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(0,1),(1,0)\}\) and let \(G=\{e,g\}\), where \(g(x_1,x_2)=(x_2,x_1)\). The set \(X\) is one \(G\)-orbit. The restrictions \(R_+=\{x:x_1\ge x_2\}\) and \(R_-=\{x:x_1\le x_2\}\) each retain exactly one point of that orbit when imposed separately. Their simultaneous imposition requires \(x_1=x_2\), so \(X\cap R_+\cap R_-=\varnothing\). Hence individually valid representative conventions on overlapping support can jointly delete an entire feasible orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two swapped binary variables, opposite ordering conventions are separately valid but together eliminate both asymmetric feasible points and therefore the whole orbit.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Representative Conflicts

children.title: Presolve Symmetry Processing
children.top_down_role: Symmetry detection and handling during model presolve.

assumptions_latex: An original mixed-integer model has feasible set \(X\), objective \(f\), and known symmetry group \(G\).
Each presolve reduction supplies a reconstruction map and records how surviving symmetries act on the reduced variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \((X',f',G',\rho,\phi)\) preserves feasibility, objective values, and the recorded symmetry action.

notation.meaning: Reconstruction map from reduced to original solutions
Map relating retained original symmetries to reduced symmetries

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-aware presolve with explicit solution reconstruction and group-action tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a model with feasible set \(X\), objective \(f\), and symmetry group \(G\). Repeatedly apply a valid presolve reduction, update the reduced set \(X'\) and objective \(f'\), compose its solution-reconstruction map into \(\rho:X'\to X\), and retain only symmetries inducing well-defined permutations on the current reduced variables. Record these as a group \(G'\) with homomorphism \(\phi:G'\to G\). Stop at a presolve fixed point and output \((X',f',G',\rho,\phi)\), requiring \(f(\rho(y))=f'(y)\) and \(\rho(g'y)=\phi(g')\rho(y)\) for all \(y\in X'\) and \(g'\in G'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetry-aware presolve reduces the model while composing reconstruction maps and retaining only symmetries whose action remains well defined on reduced variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Symmetry Processing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the presolve leaf, but an inspectable specialized source is needed to determine the required solution-lifting completeness and whether a well-defined reduced-variable permutation alone suffices to retain a symmetry. The displayed conditions establish reconstruction soundness, not full presolve equivalence.

children.title: Root-Level Symmetry Processing
children.top_down_role: Symmetry restrictions and reductions applied at the root search state.

assumptions_latex: The presolved root relaxation is \(P_0\supseteq X'\), and \(G'\) preserves \(X'\) and the objective.
Every added inequality is valid for \(X'\), including any symmetry-generated image used at the root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Root processing returns a relaxation \(P_r\supseteq X'\) together with a subgroup \(G_r\le G'\) preserving all root-level state.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-node processing that synchronizes cuts, propagation, and the active symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the root relaxation as \(P_0\supseteq X'\) with active group \(G'\). Alternate root propagation, relaxation strengthening, and symmetry processing. After each state change, replace the active group by the subgroup preserving all fixed domains, added constraints, and representative conventions; when a valid inequality is propagated through symmetry, add only images valid for \(X'\). Stop when the selected root procedures reach their stopping criteria. Output a relaxation \(P_r\supseteq X'\), the root state, and a group \(G_r\le G'\) that preserves that complete state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root processing strengthens and propagates the presolved model while updating the active group to preserve all root constraints, domains, and representative conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Level Symmetry Processing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the root-processing leaf, but the stopping rule, state-preserving subgroup update, and interaction among propagation, cuts, and representative conventions require specialized solver-symmetry support.

children.title: Presolve-to-Root Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of detected structures and valid restrictions into root processing.

assumptions_latex: Presolve produces \((X',f',G',\rho,\phi)\) with an equivariant reconstruction map.
Every root-level variable, constraint, and symmetry reference has a recorded image in the presolved model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred root state is interpretable in the original model and commutes with reconstruction under the retained group action.

notation.meaning: Embedding of retained symmetries into the original action

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), the active group \(G_v\) preserves the current feasible set \(X_v\).
A branch consists of child regions \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) covering \(X_v\).

If the chosen disjunction is not globally invariant, child \(i\) must inherit only \(G_{v,i}=\{g\in G_v:gB_i=B_i\}\). children.title: Propagation-Branching Coordination
children.top_down_role: Consistency of symmetry state across propagation outcomes and tree construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Branching Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-update rule coordinating symmetry-aware propagation with subsequent branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let sound propagation replace \(D_v\) by \(D_v^+\), and let \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) be a branching disjunction covering every point of \(X_v\cap D_v^+\). Child \(i\) receives domain \(D_{v,i}=D_v^+\cap B_i\) and group \(G_{v,i}=\{g\in G_v:gD_{v,i}=D_{v,i}\}\). Propagation consequences are installed before symmetry-equivalent children are identified. Any later domain reduction or branch pruning in child \(i\) must use \(G_{v,i}\), ensuring that neither stale symmetries nor domains excluded by propagation influence the branching decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate first, branch over the remaining feasible domain, and give each child only the symmetries stabilizing its propagated branch domain.
assumptions_latex: Propagation at node \(v\) produces a sound domain \(D_v^+\subseteq D_v\).
The branching disjunction \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) covers all feasible points remaining in \(D_v^+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each child receives \(D_{v,i}=D_v^+\cap B_i\) and only the symmetries in \(G_v\) that stabilize \(D_{v,i}\).

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), \(G_v\) preserves the node-feasible set \(X_v\).
A separator returns an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) valid for \(X_v\).

Then each symmetry image \((g a)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), with coefficients transformed by the induced action, is also valid for \(X_v\). children.title: Primal-Heuristic Interfaces
