A canonicalization map \(\kappa\) preserves feasibility and objective value on every symmetry orbit.

children.title: Cross-Subsystem Consistency

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Subsystem Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for symmetry information shared by branching, cutting, conflict analysis, and primal heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(v\), let \(F_v\) be the node-feasible set, \(G_v\) an active symmetry group satisfying \(gF_v=F_v\), and \(c_v:F_v\to F_v\) a representative map. Cross-subsystem consistency holds when every participating subsystem uses this same state and, for every \(g\in G_v\) and \(x\in F_v\), \(c_v(gx)=c_v(x)\) and \(c_v(x)\in G_vx\). Any generated restriction \(R\) declared symmetry-invariant must satisfy \(gR=R\) for all \(g\in G_v\); otherwise its validity metadata must explicitly restrict the group to \(\{g\in G_v:gR=R\}\).

assumptions_latex: \(G_v\) acts on the variables and preserves \(F_v\).
Each subsystem identifies the node and version of its symmetry state.

children.title: Node-Local Group State
children.top_down_role: Residual symmetry-group information associated with an individual search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Group State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active symmetry group induced by the current node subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a group of permutations preserving the root feasible set and objective, and let \(F_v\) be the feasible set remaining at node \(v\), including local bounds and local constraints. The node-local group state is the setwise stabilizer
\[G_v:=\operatorname{Stab}_G(F_v)=\{g\in G:gF_v=F_v\}.\]
If the state stores generators rather than all elements, those generators must generate exactly \(G_v\), or a declared subgroup \(H_v\leq G_v\) when incomplete symmetry exploitation is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node-local group is the root symmetry subgroup preserving every bound and constraint currently active at that node.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on the root model's variable space.
\(F_v\) includes every node-local restriction relevant to symmetry validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_v\) is a group acting on and preserving \(F_v\).
review_flags: standard stabilizer construction but node-state interpretation needs a direct source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Node-Local Group State leaf, and the setwise stabilizer construction is mathematically standard. However, the record supplies no citation supporting its interpretation as maintained solver state or the exact-generator versus declared-subgroup requirement.

children.title: Node-Local Ordering State
children.top_down_role: Representative-ordering information associated with an individual search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Ordering State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-specific data defining canonical representatives within active symmetry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a node-feasible set \(F_v\) and active group \(G_v\), a node-local ordering state is a pair \((\preceq_v,c_v)\), where \(\preceq_v\) is a total order on \(F_v\) or on a finite comparison encoding of its points, and
\[c_v(x):=\min_{\preceq_v}(G_vx)\]
whenever the orbit minimum exists. The state must record every tie-breaking convention needed to make \(c_v\) single-valued. If only partial canonicalization is implemented, its domain and the subgroup whose orbits are compared must be stored explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local ordering state fixes an order and tie breakers that select one canonical point from each active symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: Every orbit to be canonicalized has a \(\preceq_v\)-minimum.
The comparison encoding distinguishes points whenever unique representatives are required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(c_v\) is single-valued and selects a member of \(G_vx\) for each point in its declared domain.

notation.meaning: orbit of x under the active group

review_flags: canonical-order definition is standard but lifecycle interpretation needs a direct source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Node-Local Ordering State leaf, but no source supports this particular lifecycle interface. A source must also clarify how an order on a finite comparison encoding induces a well-defined total comparison of points when the encoding is not injective.

children.title: Group-Ordering Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between residual group information and node-local ordering choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Ordering Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate between the active node group and its canonical ordering state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_v\) preserve \(F_v\), and let \(c_v\) be induced by the node-local ordering state. Group-ordering consistency holds precisely when, for every \(x\in F_v\) and \(g\in G_v\),
\[c_v(x)\in G_vx,\qquad c_v(gx)=c_v(x),\qquad c_v(c_v(x))=c_v(x).\]
If the ordering state was inherited from an ancestor, these identities must be revalidated after replacing the ancestor group by \(G_v\). Failure of any identity forbids using \(c_v\) to discard a node or feasible point as a symmetric duplicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonicalizer is consistent with the active group exactly when it selects one idempotent, orbit-constant representative from every active orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G_vF_v=F_v\).
\(c_v\) is defined on every point to which symmetry reduction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Symmetry pruning based on \(c_v\) compares only points in the same \(G_v\)-orbit and assigns them one representative.
review_flags: formal consistency predicate needs citation in solver-symmetry literature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is appropriate for Group-Ordering Consistency, and the three displayed identities characterize an orbit-constant idempotent representative selector. No citation is supplied for treating these identities as the precise solver validity condition or for the stated pruning prohibition after inherited-state changes.

children.title: Search-Tree State-Reconstruction Boundary

children.title: Restart Behavior
children.top_down_role: Persistence or reconstruction of symmetry information after solver restarts.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving reconstruction of symmetry state after a search restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a restart replaces a search tree by a root or retained frontier with feasible regions \(F'_w\). For every surviving or newly created node \(w\), the restarted symmetry state must be reconstructed as \(G'_w=\{g\in G:gF'_w=F'_w\}\), together with a canonicalizer consistent with \(G'_w\). A cached state from an earlier node \(v\) may be reused only if its validity certificate establishes \(F_v=F'_w\) and equality of all ordering-relevant metadata. Thus restart may change search order and retained inferences, but it must not change the feasible solutions excluded solely by certified symmetry equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After restart, symmetry state must be rebuilt from retained restrictions; stale state is reusable only when its entire validity context is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The root symmetry group \(G\) remains certified for the retained model.
Every retained local or global restriction is available during reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every post-restart symmetry reduction is valid for its reconstructed node subproblem.
review_flags: restart-specific symmetry lifecycle rule needs an implementation or solver-design source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits Restart Behavior, but the restart-specific reconstruction rule has no supporting source. The requirement to reconstruct the full stabilizer conflicts with the earlier allowance for using a certified subgroup, and equality of feasible regions may not by itself characterize all solver-state validity metadata. A direct source is needed before choosing the precise formulation.

children.title: Tree-Rewrite Behavior
children.top_down_role: Validity of dynamic symmetry state after structural changes to the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Rewrite Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe transfer condition when nodes or subtrees are replaced by equivalent search regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a tree rewrite map an old node \(v\) to a new node \(w\) through a bijection \(T:F_v\to F'_w\) that preserves feasibility and objective values. An old symmetry state \((G_v,c_v)\) is transferable only when the new group is \(G'_w=TG_vT^{-1}\) and the new canonicalizer satisfies
\[c'_w\circ T=T\circ c_v.\]
For a nonbijective rewrite, cached orbit representatives or pruning decisions may be transferred only after direct revalidation on \(F'_w\); feasibility equivalence of the aggregate subtree alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rewritten subtree may inherit symmetry state only through an objective-preserving bijection that conjugates groups and commutes with canonicalization.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) preserves objective values on \(F_v\).
The old state is valid on all of \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transferred orbit equivalence and representative decisions are valid on \(F'_w\).
review_flags: conjugacy criterion is mathematically standard but tree-rewrite application needs a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer condition fits Tree-Rewrite Behavior, but no source is supplied. Requiring the new group to equal the full conjugate is stronger than necessary when a certified conjugate subgroup would suffice, so the exact necessity claim cannot be retained without authoritative support.

children.title: State Reconstruction Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases requiring symmetry state to be rebuilt rather than retained.

knowledge_statements.title: State Reconstruction Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between reconstructible symmetry facts and history-dependent search artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetry-state component is reconstructible at node \(v\) if it is a deterministic function of the certified root model, the complete active restriction set defining \(F_v\), and declared ordering metadata. The group \(G_v=\{g\in G:gF_v=F_v\}\) and a deterministically specified canonicalizer are reconstructible. Cached orbit tables, incremental stabilizer chains, timestamps, and prior pruning decisions are not reconstructible unless their derivation certificates are retained. Beyond this boundary, replaying an uncertified historical artifact may eliminate a point without establishing that its representative remains feasible in the current node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Groups and deterministic canonicalizers can be rebuilt from the current model; historical caches require retained derivation certificates before reuse.
assumptions_latex: The current node restriction set is complete.
The root group and ordering metadata have valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only reconstructible components or separately certified historical artifacts may authorize symmetry pruning after state loss.
review_flags: reconstruction boundary is an interface specification lacking direct supplied evidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind matches the leaf, but the division between reconstructible state and history-dependent artifacts is an uncited solver-interface specification. In particular, the certificate requirements for caches, stabilizer chains, and prior pruning decisions need direct implementation or verification literature.

children.title: Cross-Instance Symmetry Transfer Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transfer boundaries for symmetry information in auxiliary solver instances and decomposed solves.

children.title: Subproblem Transfer Behavior
children.top_down_role: Transfer of symmetry information into restricted or auxiliary subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Transfer Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivariant transfer of symmetry state from a parent model to a derived subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a source feasible set with symmetry group \(G\), and let \(T:F'\to F\) embed a target subproblem. A subgroup \(H\leq G\) transfers to the target only if \(hT(F')=T(F')\) for every \(h\in H\) and there exists an action \(\rho:H\to\operatorname{Sym}(F')\) satisfying
\[T(\rho(h)x)=hT(x)\]
for all \(h\in H\) and \(x\in F'\). Objective values must also be preserved under this action. Source canonicalization transfers only when it maps \(T(F')\) into itself and its conjugate through \(T\) is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source symmetry transfers to a subproblem only when the embedding is equivariant and the subgroup preserves the embedded feasible region and objective.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is injective on \(F'\).
\(H\) preserves the source objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(H)\) acts by objective-preserving symmetries of the target subproblem.
review_flags: equivariant transfer formulation needs a direct optimization-symmetry source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivariant-transfer condition is mathematically plausible and fits Subproblem Transfer Behavior, but no cited source supports this exact optimization-interface formulation. An authoritative source should establish the required subgroup restriction, induced action, objective preservation, and canonicalizer-transfer conditions.

children.title: Solver-Copy Behavior
children.top_down_role: Preservation of symmetry structures in copied solver instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Copy Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-state preservation under an isomorphic copy of a solver model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X'\) be the variable-value bijection used to copy a solver instance, with \(x\in F\) if and only if \(T(x)\in F'\), and with equal objective values at corresponding points. If \(G\) is a certified symmetry group of the source, then the copied group must be
\[G'=TGT^{-1}.\]
Every generator, canonicalizer, affected-variable index, and certificate reference must be translated through \(T\). Copying raw variable identifiers or cached node-local states without this translation does not establish symmetry validity in the destination instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isomorphic solver copy preserves symmetry only by conjugating every group action and translating all state and certificates through the copy map.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a bijection between the source and destination variable-value spaces.
\(T\) preserves feasibility and objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G'\) is a certified symmetry group of the copied instance, and translated canonicalization preserves corresponding orbits.
review_flags: copy-lifecycle requirement needs documentation from a symmetry-aware solver

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits Solver-Copy Behavior and conjugation under an instance isomorphism is standard. Nevertheless, the requirements concerning generators, indices, cached state, and certificate references are implementation-level claims without an inspectable solver source.

children.title: Decomposition Behavior
children.top_down_role: Distribution of symmetry information across decomposed solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for combining or restricting symmetries across decomposed model blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) and the decomposed feasible set is a Cartesian product \(F=F_1\times\cdots\times F_k\) with additively separable objective. Then independently certified block groups \(G_i\) induce the product action \(G_1\times\cdots\times G_k\) on \(F\). If coupling constraints or shared master variables are present, only the subgroup of this product that preserves every coupling relation is a symmetry of the full model. Consequently, independent block canonicalization is invalid when it maps a feasible coupled tuple to one violating a coupling constraint or changes the master-dependent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block symmetries combine as a product only for genuinely separable models; coupling restricts them to the subgroup preserving all cross-block relations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(G_i\) preserves \(F_i\) and its block objective.
The asserted product case has no omitted coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full-model group is the product in the separable case and a coupling stabilizer subgroup otherwise.

notation.meaning: certified symmetry group of block i

review_flags: supplied decomposition locators do not directly support the symmetry-transfer boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is suitable, but the supplied inventory contains no symmetry-transfer source. Moreover, the product of certified block groups is a symmetry group in the separable case, not necessarily the full-model symmetry group, since additional symmetries such as exchanges of isomorphic blocks may exist. The exact conclusion requires correction supported by a direct source.

children.title: Cross-Instance Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on reusing symmetry information outside its originating solver instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance Validity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary boundary for reusing symmetry claims between distinct optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let source and target instances have feasible sets \(F,F'\) and objectives \(f,f'\). A source symmetry action may be reused in the target only when a certified bijection \(T:F\to F'\) satisfies \(f'(T(x))=f(x)\) and transports the action by conjugation. More generally, transfer to a restricted target requires a certified invariant embedding and subgroup restriction. Equality of dimensions, variable names, matrix sparsity patterns, or decomposition layouts alone is insufficient: if feasibility or objective preservation fails for some transported generator, the transferred group, orbit representatives, and all pruning decisions depending on them are invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-instance reuse ends unless a certified isomorphism or invariant embedding preserves feasibility, objectives, and the transported group action.
assumptions_latex: The transfer is intended to justify solution-eliminating symmetry reductions.
All target-side model transformations affecting feasibility or objectives are represented in the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only certified conjugate actions, or certified restricted actions, remain valid across instances.
review_flags: cross-instance certification boundary needs a direct source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits Cross-Instance Validity Boundary, and the isomorphism and invariant-embedding distinctions are plausible. No direct source supports the certificate obligations or the invalidation of all dependent cached representatives and pruning decisions.

children.title: Symmetry Detection Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for validating claimed symmetry actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Detection Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite witness for checking that claimed generators preserve an integer optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer model \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\}\), a symmetry-detection certificate consists of permutations \(S=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_m\}\) and checkable witnesses that, for every \(\pi\in S\), variable domains are transported compatibly, \(x\in F\) if and only if \(\pi x\in F\), and \(f(\pi x)=f(x)\). For a finite algebraic model representation, these obligations may be certified by explicit permutations of variables, constraints, coefficients, bounds, and objective terms. Successful verification certifies every element of \(\langle S\rangle\) as an objective-preserving symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A detection certificate lists generators and verifiable mappings showing that each preserves domains, constraints, and the objective; their generated group is then certified.
assumptions_latex: The model representation has exact, decidable equality for all compared data.
Each listed permutation acts bijectively on variable assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(g\in\langle S\rangle\) satisfies \(gF=F\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\).
review_flags: certificate interface is precise but supplied sources do not address symmetry detection certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind exactly fits the Symmetry Detection Certificates topic, and generator closure would certify the generated group once every generator is verified. However, no cited source defines this certificate interface or establishes which finite representation mappings suffice to verify semantic preservation of domains, feasibility, and objective values.

children.title: Representative-Dominance Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for static and dynamic representative restrictions.

children.title: Representative Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for restrictions selecting symmetry representatives.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is the feasible set and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is minimized.
A finite group \(G\) acts on \(X\), with \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified point is a valid canonical representative of the orbit \(Gx\).

notation.meaning: Canonical-representative predicate, true for exactly one point of each relevant orbit.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit membership plus a uniquely selecting canonical predicate is a directly checkable representative certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static orbit-representative certificate for an invariant integer minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representative certificate for \(x\in X\) is a pair \((r,g)\in X\times G\) satisfying \(r=gx\), \(R(r)=1\), and \(\sum_{y\in Gx}R(y)=1\). Verification consists of checking group membership of \(g\), the equality \(r=gx\), feasibility of \(r\), and the canonical predicate. Because the action preserves feasibility and objective value, \(r\in Gx\subseteq X\) and \(f(r)=f(x)\); uniqueness of \(R\) identifies \(r\) as the selected representative of \(Gx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group element maps the point to the unique orbit member satisfying the canonical rule, while preserving feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Representative Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and orbit-representative claim are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports this specific certificate formulation or its verification requirements.

children.title: Dominance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for symmetry-based dominance decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is feasible and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is minimized.
The admissible transformations preserve feasibility and do not increase the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dominated point may be discarded without removing all optimal solutions.

notation.meaning: Set of points retained by the representative rule.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a feasible non-worsening image in the retained region is a checkable dominance witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance witness for eliminating a nonrepresentative feasible integer point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\setminus C\), a dominance certificate is a transformation \(g\) and point \(y=gx\) such that \(y\in C\cap X\) and \(f(y)\leq f(x)\). The verifier checks that \(g\) is admissible, that \(y=gx\), that \(y\) satisfies the model constraints and representative rule, and that the objective inequality holds. Thus every certified excluded point has a retained feasible image of no worse value, so excluding \(x\) cannot increase the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discarded point is dominated when a verifiable admissible transformation sends it to a retained feasible point with no worse objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The non-worsening retained-image condition is coherent for minimization, but the symmetry/dominance certificate formulation has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Dynamic Representative Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certification of representative restrictions dependent on the current search state.

assumptions_latex: A search node \(u\) has completion set \(X_u\subseteq X\).
The node stabilizer \(G_u\) preserves \(X_u\) and the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate validates the representative relative to the current search-node symmetry.

notation.meaning: Subgroup preserving the decisions at node u.
Feasible completions compatible with node u.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dynamic representatives must be certified under the current node stabilizer rather than the root group
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-relative representative certificate under a dynamically changing stabilizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(u\), a dynamic representative certificate for \(x\in X_u\) is \((r,g,G_u)\) satisfying \(g\in G_u\), \(r=gx\in X_u\), \(R_u(r)=1\), and \(\sum_{y\in G_ux}R_u(y)=1\). It additionally records generators for \(G_u\) and checkable evidence that each generator preserves the node decisions. Verification therefore establishes \(f(r)=f(x)\) and that \(r\) is the unique selected member of the node-relative orbit \(G_ux\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate identifies the unique representative under the subgroup that preserves all decisions at the current search node.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Representative Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-relative certificate fits the leaf, but sources are required for the claimed generator evidence, stabilizer validation, and dynamic representative semantics.

children.title: Search-Reduction Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for symmetry-aware branching, pruning, and domain reduction.

children.title: Branching Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for symmetry-aware branching decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-covering certificate for symmetry-reduced branching at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching certificate for children \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) provides checkable evidence that \[X_u\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k G_uX_{u_i},\qquad G_uX_{u_i}:=\{gx:g\in G_u,\ x\in X_{u_i}\}.\] Equivalently, for every \(x\in X_u\), it identifies \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(g\in G_u\), and \(z\in X_{u_i}\) such that \(x=gz\). The verifier checks the child constraints, group membership, and the stated cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The children are valid when their symmetry images cover every feasible completion of the parent node, ensuring that every parent orbit meets a searched child.
assumptions_latex: Node \(u\) has completion set \(X_u\) and objective-preserving stabilizer \(G_u\).
Children \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) have completion sets \(X_{u_i}\subseteq X_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Searching the certified children retains at least one member of every \(G_u\)-orbit in \(X_u\).

notation.meaning: Feasible completions at search node u.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit-covering of a parent completion set is the necessary checkable condition for symmetry-reduced branching

children.title: Domain-Reduction Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for symmetry-based domain reductions.

assumptions_latex: Node \(u\) has completion set \(X_u\) and objective-preserving stabilizer \(G_u\).
A proposed reduction replaces a domain \(D_j\) by \(D'_j\subseteq D_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing \(D_j\setminus D'_j\) preserves an optimal completion of node \(u\), if one exists.

notation.meaning: Original and reduced domains of variable j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: each removed completion requires a retained orbit-equivalent or dominating completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-aware certificate for deleting values from an integer variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A domain-reduction certificate establishes that for every \(x\in X_u\) with \(x_j\in D_j\setminus D'_j\), there exist \(g_x\in G_u\) and \(y=g_xx\in X'_u\) with \(f(y)\leq f(x)\). The quantified claim may be represented by an exhaustive finite table or a separately checkable symbolic rule. Verification checks coverage of all removed values, admissibility of each transformation, feasibility of every image, and the objective comparison. Hence some optimal completion remains in \(X'_u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every completion using a deleted value must have a retained symmetry image or dominating completion with no worse objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Reduction Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified retained-image condition is sufficient for the stated minimization conclusion, but the proposed certificate representations and verification procedure lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Pruning Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces for symmetry-based search pruning.

assumptions_latex: Node \(u\) has feasible completion set \(X_u\).
An incumbent value \(U\) is available for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node \(u\) can be pruned without losing a solution improving upon \(U\).

notation.meaning: A valid lower bound on the node.
An already retained or explored completion set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bound pruning and dominance-to-retained-region are independently verifiable pruning alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for bound-based or symmetry-dominance pruning of a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pruning certificate for node \(u\) has either of two forms. A bound certificate gives a valid \(L_u\) with \(f(x)\geq L_u\geq U\) for every \(x\in X_u\). A symmetry-dominance certificate gives a retained or explored set \(Y\subseteq X\) and, for every \(x\in X_u\), a checkable admissible transformation producing \(y\in Y\) with \(f(y)\leq f(x)\). Either form proves that node \(u\) contains no necessary solution better than the incumbent or retained search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is prunable when a verified bound reaches the incumbent or every completion is dominated by an already retained symmetry image.
knowledge_statements.title: Pruning Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both certificate alternatives plausibly fit pruning, but no source supports the combined bound-or-symmetry certificate specification or the exact retained-region requirements.

children.title: Certificate Composition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on combining branching, reduction, and pruning justifications.

assumptions_latex: Each local search reduction is valid for the completion set and symmetry subgroup recorded at its application node.
Certificates are composed along a root-to-descendant path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local certificates compose only when every witness remains admissible after all intervening search restrictions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local orbit witnesses cease to compose when later constraints invalidate their images or transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for composing branching, reduction, and pruning certificates across search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v\succeq u\), a certificate at \(u\) composes with descendant certificates only if every transformation used on \(X_v\) belongs to \(G_v\), maps \(X_v\) into the completion set claimed by the next certificate, and preserves the objective comparison. Membership merely in \(G_u\) is insufficient. If some \(g\in G_u\setminus G_v\) maps a descendant completion outside \(X_v\), then a representative, dominance, or pruning witness using \(g\) cannot be transferred to \(v\) without revalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificates compose only while their transformations preserve every later node restriction; an ancestor symmetry alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Composition Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the container, but the asserted necessity of descendant-stabilizer membership and the transfer conditions need a symmetry-specific source; ancestor membership alone is not enough to establish the exact boundary.

children.title: Method Applicability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determining which symmetry-handling families apply.

children.title: Variable-Domain Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Applicability boundaries arising from variable-domain assumptions.

children.title: Binary-Domain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Symmetry-handling applicability under binary-variable assumptions.

assumptions_latex: All integer variables satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
A group \(G\leq S_n\) acts by permuting coordinates and preserves feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orbit-based representative restrictions are valid on the binary feasible set.

notation.meaning: Action of a permutation on a vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coordinate permutations automatically preserve a common binary product domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability predicate for coordinate-permutation symmetry methods on binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The binary-domain regime holds when \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \((gx)_i=x_{g^{-1}(i)}\) for every \(g\in G\), \(gX=X\), and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Because every coordinate has the common domain \(\{0,1\}\), the action is domain preserving. Any restriction selecting at least one member from every orbit \(Gx\) is then complete, and a restriction selecting exactly one member is a symmetry-breaking representative system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary symmetry methods apply when coordinate permutations preserve the feasible set and objective; the common binary domain is automatically preserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Domain Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is coherent for coordinate-permutation symmetries on a binary feasible set, but no cited source supports the completeness and representative-system claims.

children.title: General-Domain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability across bounded integer, mixed-domain, or broader variable settings.

knowledge_statements.title: General-Domain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability predicate for symmetry methods beyond common binary domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The general-domain regime holds when every \(g\in G\) is a bijection \(D\to D\), satisfies \(gX=X\), and obeys \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). For a coordinate permutation, domain preservation additionally requires \(D_i=D_{g(i)}\) for every moved coordinate, unless the action includes certified value bijections \(D_i\to D_{g(i)}\). Under these conditions, every orbit of a feasible point lies in \(X\) and has constant objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonbinary domains, every symmetry must bijectively preserve compatible variable domains as well as the feasible set and objective value; representative selection can then preserve the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The variable domain is the finite product \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\).
The feasible set is \(X\subseteq D\), and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the objective function.
A finite group \(G\) acts on \(D\) by explicitly represented bijections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orbit-based symmetry reduction is valid under domain, feasibility, and objective invariance.

notation.meaning: Product of possibly nonbinary variable domains.
Feasible subset of the product domain.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: general-domain symmetry requires bijective preservation of domains, feasibility, and objective

children.title: Domain-Extension Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring binary-specific handling to more general domains.

assumptions_latex: A proposed transformation \(g\) is used to identify solutions of an integer model.
The feasible set satisfies \(X\subseteq D=\prod_iD_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orbit reduction is unjustified beyond the boundary where \(g\) fails to preserve the feasible domain and objective.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit deletion requires a genuine objective-preserving self-bijection of the feasible set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp validity boundary when extending binary symmetry methods to heterogeneous domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A binary-domain symmetry method extends to \(D\) only if each proposed \(g\) restricts to an objective-preserving bijection \(X	o X\). Failure occurs when some \(x\in X\) has \(gx
otin D\), \(gx
otin X\), or \(f(gx)
eq f(x)\). For example, swapping coordinates with domains \(D_1=\{0,1\}\) and \(D_2=\{0,1,2\}\) sends \((0,2)\) to \((2,0)
otin D_1	imes D_2\). Orbit-based deletion using that swap can therefore remove a nonreplaceable feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension fails when a proposed symmetry leaves the product domain, violates feasibility, or changes objective value; heterogeneous domains expose this boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Extension Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly exhibits failure of product-domain preservation, but the claimed sharp boundary and resulting nonreplaceability require a source addressing exact symmetry reduction rather than broader dominance reductions.

children.title: Group-Structure Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Specialized matrix or object actions versus generic detected groups.

children.title: Structured-Group Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability for matrix, object, or other explicitly structured group actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Group Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability condition for methods exploiting a recognized group decomposition or standard action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured-group regime is present when a certificate identifies a \(G\)-invariant block system \(\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\), relevant component groups, and a verified isomorphism expressing \(G\) through a supported construction, such as a direct product or wreath product, whose induced action agrees with the action on \(X\). Every certified generator must preserve feasibility and objective value. A representative or propagation method is applicable only when it is valid for the certified construction and its induced component actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group is in a structured regime when a verified standard decomposition and its induced action match the model action and support the proposed componentwise reasoning.
assumptions_latex: A finite symmetry group \(G\) acts on the feasible set \(X\).
The representation exposes a recognized decomposition or standard action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Symmetry reasoning may operate componentwise only through the certified structural decomposition and a method valid for that structure.

notation.meaning: A block system preserved setwise by the group action.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exploitable group structure must include a checkable decomposition and compatible action on model variables

children.title: Generic-Group Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability for groups represented primarily through detected generators.

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(G\) is supplied by generators acting on the model variables.
Generator actions preserve the feasible set \(X\) and objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only methods requiring generator access and general group operations are justified without further structural recognition.

notation.meaning: Feasible set preserved by the action.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a generator-defined group supports generic group algorithms but not structure-specific deductions without a recognition certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability condition when symmetry is known only through a generic generating set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generic-group regime holds when \(G=\langle S\rangle\) is specified by generators, every \(s\in S\) satisfies \(sX=X\) and \(f(sx)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\), but no supported structural decomposition of \(G\) is certified. Orbit, stabilizer, and membership procedures valid for generator-defined finite groups remain applicable. Conclusions requiring a direct-product, wreath-product, full-symmetric, or other special action are not certified merely by the generator representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With only verified generators, generic orbit and stabilizer methods apply, but structure-specific methods require an additional recognition certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic-Group Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic-group condition is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but the applicability claims for orbit, stabilizer, and membership procedures require a source specifying the group representation and supported algorithms.

children.title: Structure-Recognition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Consequences of failing to expose specialized structure inside a generic group representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Recognition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between certified formulation symmetries and merely apparent repeated structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(G\leq S_n\) act by coordinate permutations. A detected subgroup \(H\leq G\) is certified for symmetry handling only if, for every \(h\in H\), \(hX=X\) and \(f(hx)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Repeated coefficients, blocks, or graph patterns that do not establish both identities lie beyond the recognition boundary: constraints selecting unequal domains, bounds, integrality types, or objective coefficients can destroy the apparent permutation symmetry. Symmetry reduction based on an uncertified permutation may therefore remove every optimal representative of an orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recognized permutation is usable only when it preserves feasibility and objective values; superficial repeated structure is insufficient and unsafe symmetry breaking may remove all optima.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
The action of \(S_n\) permutes decision-variable coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) is sound for symmetry reduction only if \(hX=X\) and \(f\circ h=f\) for every \(h\in H\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the integer or mixed-integer model
detected subgroup proposed for symmetry handling

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formulation symmetry requires preservation of the feasible set and objective
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the terminal container, and feasible-set plus objective invariance is the standard certification condition. No cited source supports either that condition or the stated consequence of unsafe symmetry reduction, so source review is required.

children.title: Symmetry-Scope Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Globally valid actions versus locally activated symmetry.

children.title: Global-Symmetry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Handling regimes for symmetry valid throughout the model or search.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Symmetry Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability condition for symmetry methods valid throughout the complete feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optimization problem \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\), a group \(G\) is a global symmetry group when it acts on the ambient variable space and satisfies \(gX=X\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in X\). Consequently, each orbit \(Gx=\{gx:g\in G\}\) is either contained in \(X\) or disjoint from it, and all feasible members of an orbit have the same objective value. Any constraint selecting at least one representative from every feasible orbit is therefore globally valid as a symmetry-breaking restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global symmetry preserves the entire feasible set and objective, so one representative may be retained from every feasible orbit without changing the optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts bijectively on the ambient variable space.
\(X\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting at least one point from each feasible orbit preserves the optimal value.

notation.meaning: orbit of a point under the group action

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global optimization symmetry is defined by feasible-set and objective invariance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and global-orbit statement fit the container and are mathematically coherent. The record has no inspectable citation for global formulation symmetry or orbit-representative validity.

children.title: Subsymmetry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Handling regimes for symmetry activated only in restricted states or substructures.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsymmetry Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local symmetry condition on a restricted search region or branch-and-bound subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_u\subseteq X\) be the feasible region remaining at a search node or within an activated subproblem. A group \(G_u\) is a subsymmetry group on \(X_u\) if \(gX_u=X_u\) and \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G_u\) and \(x\in X_u\), even when some \(g\in G_u\) fails to preserve all of \(X\). Orbit-representative restrictions derived from \(G_u\) are valid within \(X_u\), provided they retain a representative of every \(G_u\)-orbit in \(X_u\); they need not be valid outside that region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subsymmetry preserves only a restricted subproblem. Its symmetry-breaking constraints are valid locally but may cut feasible or optimal points elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: \(X_u\subseteq X\) is the complete feasible region under the current local restrictions.
\(G_u\) acts bijectively on the ambient variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Representative enforcement for \(G_u\) is valid on \(X_u\) but is not thereby valid on \(X\).

notation.meaning: subsymmetry group active on that region

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subsymmetry is symmetry of a restricted subproblem rather than the complete model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes symmetry of a restricted feasible region from global symmetry and fits the subsymmetry-regime leaf. A symmetry-specific source with a precise locator is still required.

children.title: Activation-Scope Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits separating globally valid actions from locally valid symmetry actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Scope Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary governing where locally activated symmetry restrictions remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_u\subseteq X\) be activated by a predicate \(a_u(x)=1\), and let \(G_u\) preserve \(X_u\) and the objective there. A symmetry-breaking predicate \(B_u\) derived from \(G_u\) may be enforced under the implication \(a_u(x)=1\Rightarrow B_u(x)\), provided every \(G_u\)-orbit in \(X_u\) contains a point satisfying \(B_u\). Enforcing \(B_u\) without its activation condition crosses the scope boundary unless \(G_u\) is also a global symmetry and \(B_u\) retains a representative of every global orbit. Otherwise globally feasible or uniquely optimal points may be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local symmetry breaker must be guarded by its activation condition unless the symmetry and representative guarantee extend to the full model.
assumptions_latex: \(G_u\) is a symmetry group of the restricted problem on \(X_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_u(x)=1\Rightarrow B_u(x)\) is locally sound; unguarded enforcement requires a separate global-validity certificate.

notation.meaning: group active within the local region

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity of a conditional reduction is confined to the region satisfying its antecedent
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the activation-scope leaf, and the guarded representative condition is plausible. No citation supports the conditional enforcement rule or the claimed failure outside the activated region.
