children.title: Linear-Model Regimes
children.top_down_role: Symmetry-handling applicability in linear integer models.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-symmetry condition for mixed-integer linear models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ \ell\leq x\leq u,\ x_j\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for }j\in I\}\) with objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). A permutation matrix \(P\) is a linear-model symmetry if \(PX=X\) and \(P^{\mathsf T}c=c\). A readily checkable formulation certificate consists of a row-permutation matrix \(Q\) satisfying \(AP=QA\), \(Qb=b\), together with preservation by \(P\) of \(\ell\), \(u\), and the index set \(I\). Under these conditions, \(x\mapsto Px\) maps every feasible solution to an equal-valued feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable permutation is a linear-model symmetry when it preserves constraints, bounds, integrality types, and the objective; compatible row permutations provide a certificate.
assumptions_latex: All model data are finite-dimensional.
\(P\) and \(Q\) are permutation matrices of compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed certificate implies \(PX=X\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}Px=c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in X\).
review_flags: locator_supports_model_class; symmetry-specific certificate needs source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the linear-model regime, and the displayed row-permutation certificate is mathematically plausible when preservation of bounds and integrality means setwise invariance. The cited chapter supports the model class but is not identified as supporting the symmetry certificate, so the substantive claim remains unsourced.

children.title: Nonlinear-Model Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation-sensitive applicability in nonlinear integer models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-symmetry condition for mixed-integer nonlinear models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=\{x\in D:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m,\ h_k(x)=0\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,r\}\), where \(D\) includes bounds and integrality restrictions. A bijection \(p:D\to D\) is a nonlinear-model symmetry if \(f(px)=f(x)\) and there are permutations \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\) satisfying \(g_{\sigma(i)}(px)=g_i(x)\) and \(h_{\tau(k)}(px)=h_k(x)\) for every admissible \(x\). These identities imply \(pX=X\). Equality only on sampled points, or preservation of the objective without preservation of the nonlinear feasible set, does not certify symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear symmetry must preserve the domain, objective, and full constraint system, possibly by permuting constraints; agreement on sampled points is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: All functions are defined on the common domain \(D\).
The map \(p\) preserves bounds and integrality restrictions encoded by \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identities imply \(pX=X\) and equal objective values on corresponding feasible points.

notation.meaning: permutations of inequality and equality constraints

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

review_flags: locator_supports_model_class; symmetry-specific condition needs source confirmation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the nonlinear-model regime, and the stated identities consistently preserve the complete constraint system. The cited section concerns classification of nonlinear integer formulations rather than the asserted symmetry criterion, leaving the mathematical claim without adequate evidence.

children.title: Conic-Model Regimes
children.top_down_role: Applicability in integer models with conic representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry certificate for a mixed-integer conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in D:Ax-b\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(D\) contains bounds and integrality restrictions. Suppose \(P\) preserves \(D\), and an invertible linear map \(R\) satisfies \(R(K)=K\), \(AP=RA\), \(Rb=b\), and \(P^{\mathsf T}c=c\). Then \(x\mapsto Px\) is a symmetry of \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X\}\), because \(A(Px)-b=R(Ax-b)\). Cone preservation by \(R\) is essential; invariance of the coefficient pattern alone does not preserve conic feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic symmetry couples a variable permutation with a cone automorphism preserving the affine conic constraint, domain, and objective.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
\(P\) and \(R\) are invertible linear maps of compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated identities imply \(PX=X\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}Px=c^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: cone automorphism acting on constraint space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine conic feasibility is preserved by an intertwining cone automorphism
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the conic-model regime, and the intertwining identities yield the displayed conic-feasibility invariance if preservation of the domain is setwise. No conic-symmetry or cone-automorphism source is cited.

children.title: Representation-Transfer Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on carrying symmetry conclusions across alternative model representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Transfer Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for transferring symmetries and symmetry breakers across reformulations or lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde X\) be a reformulation of \(X\) with projection \(\pi:\widetilde X\to X\). A lifted symmetry \(\widetilde g\) transfers to an original-space symmetry \(g\) only when \(\pi\circ\widetilde g=g\circ\pi\) on \(\widetilde X\), and the projected objective is invariant. A representative restriction on \(\widetilde X\) transfers safely only if its retained lifted representatives project to at least one representative of every relevant orbit in \(X\). If the commutation identity fails, or the restriction eliminates every point in a projection fiber, lifted symmetry breaking may alter the projected feasible set or optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetry transfers across a reformulation only through a commuting projection, and lifted representative selection must preserve every relevant projected orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi(\widetilde X)=X\).
The reformulated objective agrees with the original objective after projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of equivariance or fiber coverage invalidates automatic transfer of lifted symmetry-breaking restrictions.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the reformulated or lifted model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equivariance is the standard condition for descending a group action through a projection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the representation-transfer leaf. The equivariance and projection-fiber conditions are plausible, but no source establishes the precise descent and representative-coverage requirements, and the necessary action assumptions on the projected map require confirmation.

children.title: Symmetry-Handling Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity sources specific to detection, group processing, enforcement, and representation.

children.title: Group-Processing Complexity Family
children.top_down_role: Computational cost of generator discovery, orbit processing, and stabilizer operations.

children.title: Automorphism-Discovery Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost of discovering symmetry generators from the model representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Automorphism-Discovery Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary for discovering formulation automorphisms through graph encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a formulation is encoded faithfully as a vertex-colored graph with \(N\) vertices, so that color-preserving graph automorphisms correspond exactly to formulation symmetries. Computing generators of the formulation-symmetry group is then polynomial-time reducible to colored graph automorphism. Conversely, graph automorphism embeds into this discovery task for unrestricted faithful encodings; hence a general polynomial-time guarantee would imply one for graph automorphism. Known graph-isomorphism machinery yields a quasipolynomial bound \(N^{O(\log N)}\) for the unrestricted encoded problem, while structured graph classes can admit polynomial-time discovery. Encoding construction time must be added to this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General symmetry discovery is graph-automorphism hard after faithful encoding and admits quasipolynomial worst-case processing, while structured graph classes may be polynomial.
assumptions_latex: The graph encoding is faithful and has size polynomial in the formulation input length.
Vertex colors encode all distinctions that transformations must preserve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unrestricted discovery has bound \(N^{O(\log N)}\) via graph-isomorphism methods and no unconditional polynomial bound follows from the encoding alone.

notation.meaning: number of vertices in the faithful colored-graph encoding

review_flags: authoritative graph-isomorphism complexity theorem and reduction locator required
exact encoding assumptions require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is the correct role for this leaf, but the graph-automorphism equivalence and the exact bound \(N^{O(\log N)}\) require authoritative theorem and reduction locators. The unrestricted converse also depends on a formally specified encoding class, so the claimed complexity version is not reliable without sources.

children.title: Orbit-Processing Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost of computing and maintaining orbit information.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Processing Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of computing a point orbit from explicit permutation generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\langle S\rangle\leq S_n\), where each generator in \(S\) is stored as an explicit length-\(n\) permutation array. For any point \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), breadth-first traversal starting from \(i\) and applying every generator to each newly discovered point computes \(G i\). Because at most \(n\) points are discovered and each generator application to a point takes constant time, the traversal uses \(O(n|S|)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space. If complete images of all orbit elements under all generators are stored, the storage becomes \(O(n|S|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With explicit generators, a point orbit is found by graph traversal in linear time in the degree times the generator count.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is an explicit generating set for \(G\leq S_n\).
A generator image of one point is accessible in constant time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A point orbit is computable in \(O(n|S|)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space.

notation.meaning: orbit of point i under G

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: breadth-first search of the generator-induced orbit graph gives the displayed bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the orbit-processing leaf, and the stated breadth-first traversal bound is coherent under constant-time point-image access. No permutation-group algorithm source with a precise locator is supplied.

children.title: Stabilizer-Processing Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost of operations involving stabilizers and residual groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilizer-Processing Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schreier-generator cost for a one-point stabilizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\langle S\rangle\leq S_n\), fix \(i\), and compute the orbit \(Gi\) with a transversal \(t_y\in G\) satisfying \(t_y(i)=y\). Schreier's construction forms \(t_{s(y)}^{-1}s t_y\) for each \(y\in Gi\) and \(s\in S\); these permutations generate the stabilizer \(G_i=\{g\in G:g(i)=i\}\). There are at most \(n|S|\) candidates. With explicit length-\(n\) permutation arrays, forming all candidates costs \(O(n^2|S|)\) time and \(O(n^2|S|)\) output space before redundancy removal; orbit and transversal construction costs \(O(n|S|)\) point operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schreier’s construction produces at most n times the generator count stabilizer generators, with quadratic-degree time when full permutations are explicitly materialized.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) explicitly generates \(G\leq S_n\).
Permutation composition and inversion cost \(O(n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A generating multiset for \(G_i\) is constructible in \(O(n^2|S|)\) time before redundancy removal.

notation.meaning: chosen transversal element mapping i to y

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Schreier generators are indexed by orbit points and input generators
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the stabilizer-processing leaf. The Schreier generator count and explicit-array cost are plausible under the stated conventions, but both the generator formula and the materialization cost need a cited permutation-group source and explicit cost-model support.

children.title: Representative-Enforcement Complexity Family
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes for enforcing representatives and testing canonical search states.

children.title: Separation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes for separating violated representative restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of separating explicitly enumerated lex-leader symmetry inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\leq S_n\) be supplied by an explicit list of its elements, and order vectors lexicographically. At a candidate \(x\), separation of the lex-leader system \(x\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}gx\) for all \(g\in G\) is performed by scanning every \(g\), comparing \(x\) with \(gx\), and returning any \(g\) for which \(gx\succ_{\mathrm{lex}}x\). Explicit permutation arrays give \(O(n|G|)\) time and \(O(n)\) working space. This bound is polynomial in the explicit group listing but may be exponential in a compact generator encoding because \(|G|\) can be exponential in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scanning an explicitly listed group separates lex-leader constraints in O(n|G|) time, but this can be exponential relative to a compact generator representation.
assumptions_latex: Every \(g\in G\) is available as an explicit length-\(n\) permutation array.
Lexicographic comparison examines at most \(n\) coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit-list separation costs \(O(n|G|)\), with no polynomial-in-generator-size guarantee supplied by this enumeration method.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct enumeration performs one length-n comparison per group element
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the separation leaf, and direct scanning has the stated cost for an explicitly enumerated group. No source supports the lex-leader separation formulation or its representation-sensitive complexity distinction.

children.title: Propagation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes for symmetry-aware domain propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case cost of domain-consistency propagation for representative-enforcing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be finite, let \(R\subseteq X\) contain one representative of every symmetry orbit, and let \(C_R\) be constraints satisfying \(X\cap C_R=R\). For a product domain \(D=D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\), propagation returns \(D'_i=\{v\in D_i:\exists x\in D\cap C_R,\ x_i=v\}\). The propagation complexity \(T_{\mathrm{prop}}(C_R,L)\) is the maximum running time required to compute all \(D'_i\) over encoded instances of length at most \(L\); it is polynomially bounded when \(T_{\mathrm{prop}}(C_R,L)\leq L^k\) for some constant \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation complexity is the worst-case time needed to delete every domain value having no extension satisfying the representative constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is finite.
\(X\cap C_R=R\).
The input encoding includes \(C_R\) and the finite domains \(D_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{prop}}(C_R,L)\) measures the worst-case cost of enforcing domain consistency up to input length \(L\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports symmetry-breaking propagation complexity or this domain-consistency convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source fixes the propagation model. The record defines a complexity measure rather than an actual complexity bound, and the support test uses D∩C_R instead of explicitly restricting extensions to X∩D∩C_R.

children.title: Canonicality-Testing Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes for testing whether search states satisfy canonicality requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicality-Testing Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision complexity for testing membership in a prescribed canonical representative system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act on a finite set \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), and fix a total order \(\preceq\) on \(X\). Define \(\operatorname{can}(x)=\min_{\preceq}\{g x:g\in G\}\). The canonicality problem receives an encoded pair \((G,x)\) and decides whether \(x=\operatorname{can}(x)\). Its time complexity \(T_{\mathrm{can}}(L)\) is the maximum running time over inputs of length at most \(L\), including the chosen encoding of the action and generators of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicality-testing complexity is the worst-case time required to decide whether a point is the selected minimum of its symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts on \(X\).
\(\preceq\) is a fixed total order on \(X\).
The encoding permits evaluation of generator actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{can}}(L)\) measures the worst-case cost of deciding \(x=\operatorname{can}(x)\).

notation.meaning: least point in the orbit of x

review_flags: No supplied source identifies the intended ordering, group encoding, or canonicality-testing model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected canonicality problem or encoding. This is a definition of a complexity measure, not a complexity bound, and T_can(L) is ambiguous because X, the order, and the action representation are not consistently treated as fixed data or input.

children.title: Enforcement-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparative cost boundaries among separation, propagation, and canonicality testing.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of alternative exact representative-enforcement mechanisms by formulation and algorithmic costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq X\) be an orbit-representative system, and let \(M_1,M_2\) be exact mechanisms satisfying \(X\cap M_i=R\). Associate to \(M_i\) the cost vector \(c(M_i)=(s_i,t_i,p_i)\), where \(s_i\) is encoding size, \(t_i\) canonicality or separation time, and \(p_i\) propagation time. Mechanism \(M_1\) dominates \(M_2\) only if \(c(M_1)\leq c(M_2)\) componentwise, with at least one strict inequality. Otherwise their enforcement costs are incomparable without an application-dependent weighting or search model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact symmetry-breaking mechanisms may trade smaller formulations against cheaper testing or stronger propagation; absent componentwise dominance, no mechanism is universally cheaper.
assumptions_latex: \(X\cap M_1=X\cap M_2=R\).
All cost components use the same input encoding and computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If neither \(c(M_1)\leq c(M_2)\) nor \(c(M_2)\leq c(M_1)\), selecting between them requires an external cost criterion.

notation.meaning: size, testing, and propagation cost vector

review_flags: The cost-vector formalization is locally natural but is not supported by a supplied symmetry-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto comparison is internally plausible and fits the tradeoff leaf, but no citation supports this symmetry-specific cost vector or the selection of its three coordinates.

children.title: Representation-Proof Complexity Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Growth of representative systems, lifted formulations, and symmetry certificates.

children.title: Representative-System Size
children.top_down_role: Growth of explicit systems used to select symmetry representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative-System Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding size of constraints selecting exactly one feasible point from each orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act on \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\). A representative system is a set \(R\subseteq X\) such that \(|R\cap Gx|=1\) for every \(x\in X\). Relative to a specified constraint language \(\mathcal L\), its size is \(s_{\mathcal L}(R)=\min\{|E|:E\text{ is an }\mathcal L\text{-encoding and }X\cap E=R\}\), where \(|E|\) counts the encoded symbols or bits under the fixed convention. Size comparisons are meaningful only for the same language and encoding convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representative-system size is the shortest encoding, in a fixed constraint language, that selects exactly one feasible point from every symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts on \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\).
\(\mathcal L\) and its encoding-length convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{\mathcal L}(R)\) is the minimum encoding length of an \(\mathcal L\)-description selecting exactly \(R\) from \(X\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports this symmetry-specific encoding-size definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes this size convention. The expression X∩E=R is ill-typed because E is introduced as an encoding rather than the subset represented by that encoding; admissibility and decoding must be defined.

children.title: Lifted-Formulation Size
children.top_down_role: Growth caused by auxiliary structures in lifted symmetry formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Formulation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size of an extended formulation whose projection enforces the representative system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\). A lifted representative formulation is a mixed-integer linear system \(Ay+Bz\leq b\), with original variables \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) and auxiliary variables \(z\in\mathbb R^q\), such that \(R=\{y\in X:\exists z,\ Ay+Bz\leq b\}\). Under a fixed binary encoding, its size is the total encoding length of \((A,B,b)\), the integrality declarations, and the auxiliary dimension \(q\). The lifted-formulation size of \(R\) is the minimum such size over all admissible exact lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted-formulation size is the shortest exact extended formulation whose projection onto the original variables equals the selected representative set.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\).
Coefficient and integrality encodings are fixed.
Projection must reproduce \(R\) exactly on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted-formulation size is the minimum encoded size of any admissible system projecting exactly to \(R\) on \(X\).
review_flags: The supplied formulation references do not specifically establish lifted representative formulations for symmetry handling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and definition role align, but the quantifier domain and integrality requirements for z are unspecified. No cited source fixes the admissible lifted-formulation class or its size measure.

children.title: Proof Complexity
children.top_down_role: Size and checking burden of symmetry-reasoning certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum certificate length for validating exact representative selection in a fixed proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a proof system \(P\), a finite set \(X\), a group \(G\) acting on \(X\), and constraints \(C\). Exact representative enforcement is the assertion that every orbit \(Gx\) contains exactly one member of \(X\cap C\). Its \(P\)-proof complexity is the minimum encoded length of a \(P\)-derivation certifying both existence and uniqueness for all orbits. If no such derivation exists in \(P\), the complexity is \(+\infty\). Comparisons require the same proof system, axiom encoding, and length measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof complexity measures the shortest derivation certifying that the imposed constraints retain exactly one point from every symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(G\) are finite.
The proof system \(P\) and its encoding are fixed.
The constraints \(C\) are finitely encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complexity equals the shortest \(P\)-certificate of \(|Gx\cap X\cap C|=1\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: absence of a certificate in the proof system

review_flags: The intended proof system and certificate model are unspecified, and no supplied source resolves them.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Proof complexity depends essentially on the formal language, proof system, axioms, and encoding of the universal orbit assertion. These are not defined concretely, and no source supplies the intended model.

children.title: Compactness-Certifiability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tension between compact symmetry representations and accessible certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Compactness-Certifiability Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A representation comparison separating short encodings from short correctness certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exact representative formulation \(F\), let \(s(F)\) be its encoded size and let \(p_P(F)\) be the shortest proof, in a fixed proof system \(P\), that \(|Gx\cap X\cap F|=1\) for every \(x\in X\). Compactness and certifiability are distinct resources: from \(s(F_1)<s(F_2)\) one cannot infer \(p_P(F_1)\leq p_P(F_2)\), nor conversely. A tradeoff family is a sequence for which reducing one measure forces the other to grow under the same encoding and proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shorter symmetry-breaking formulation need not admit a shorter correctness certificate; the two resources must be measured separately.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on finite \(X\).
Each formulation selects exactly one point per orbit.
The encoding and proof system \(P\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Formulation size \(s(F)\) and certificate length \(p_P(F)\) are separate comparison coordinates unless a linking bound is established.
review_flags: No supplied source establishes a formal size-versus-certifiability tradeoff for symmetry-breaking formulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes the claimed absence of monotonicity or a formal size–certificate tradeoff. The phrase 'forces the other to grow' also lacks an indexed asymptotic definition or quantified lower bound.

children.title: Incomplete Symmetry Handling
children.top_down_role: Sources of residual equivalent search after symmetry handling.

children.title: Generator-Only Breaking Gap
children.top_down_role: Residual symmetry after imposing restrictions for selected generators only.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator-Only Breaking Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator inequalities need not enforce canonicality under the generated group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}^3\) have lexicographic order and let \(g(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x_2,x_3,x_1)\), so \(G=\langle g\rangle\) has order three. Impose only the generator restriction \(x\preceq gx\). The point \(x=(0,1,0)\) satisfies \(x\preceq gx=(1,0,0)\), but \(g^2x=(0,0,1)\prec x\). Hence \(x\) survives the generator-only restriction although it is not the canonical minimum of its \(G\)-orbit; restrictions checked only for the selected generator can leave residual symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point may compare correctly with every explicitly checked generator image yet fail against a group element formed from those generators.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{0,1\}^3\) uses lexicographic order.
\(G=\langle g\rangle\) with \(g(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x_2,x_3,x_1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=(0,1,0)\) satisfies \(x\preceq gx\) but violates \(x\preceq g^2x\), so generator-only enforcement is incomplete.
review_flags: The counterexample is directly checkable, but no supplied source documents this generator-only symmetry-breaking gap.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally checkable and fits the generator-only failure leaf, but it has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale as required by the evidence contract.

children.title: Factor-Coverage Gap Family
children.top_down_role: Residual equivalence outside handled subgroups or components.

children.title: Subgroup Coverage Gap
children.top_down_role: Residual symmetry outside the subgroup handled by the selected mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgroup Coverage Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization under a proper subgroup may leave equivalences induced by the full group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H<G\) act on a finite ordered set \(X\), and retain the \(H\)-canonical set \(R_H=\{x\in X:x\preceq hx\text{ for all }h\in H\}\). This removes all noncanonical copies within each \(H\)-orbit but is complete for \(G\) only if every \(G\)-orbit intersects \(R_H\) once. For \(X=\{0,1\}^3\), \(G=S_3\), and \(H=\langle(12)\rangle\), both \((0,0,1)\) and \((0,1,0)\) belong to \(R_H\) and lie in the same \(G\)-orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Breaking a proper subgroup can leave multiple surviving points that are equivalent under group elements outside that subgroup.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a proper subgroup of finite \(G\).
\(\preceq\) is a total order preserved as the canonicality convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Subgroup canonicalization is incomplete whenever some \(G\)-orbit contains at least two points of \(R_H\).

notation.meaning: set of points canonical under H

review_flags: The failure criterion and example are elementary but lack a supplied symmetry-specific citation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The criterion and example fit the subgroup-coverage failure leaf, but no evidence is cited. The example should also state the bit-order convention used by the lexicographic order.

children.title: Component Coverage Gap
children.top_down_role: Residual equivalence in symmetry components left untreated.

knowledge_statements.title: Component Coverage Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Omitting one direct-product symmetry component leaves its orbit multiplicities intact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times X_2\) and let \(G=G_1\times G_2\) act componentwise. Suppose restrictions select exactly one \(G_1\)-representative in each first-component orbit but impose no representative rule for \(G_2\). If some \(G_2\)-orbit in \(X_2\) has distinct points \(u\) and \(v\), then for every surviving first component \(r\), both \((r,u)\) and \((r,v)\) survive and are \(G\)-equivalent. Thus exact symmetry removal fails unless every nontrivial symmetry component is covered or otherwise rendered inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Handling only some factors of a product symmetry group leaves equivalent solutions generated by every untreated nontrivial factor.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times X_2\).
\(G=G_1\times G_2\) acts componentwise.
The restrictions constrain only the \(G_1\)-action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|G_2u|>1\) for some feasible \(u\), componentwise coverage of \(G_1\) alone cannot select one representative per \(G\)-orbit.

notation.meaning: surviving representative of a first-component orbit

review_flags: No supplied source explicitly treats incomplete coverage of direct-product symmetry components.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-group argument is plausible and fits the leaf, but no source is cited. 'Constrain only the G1-action' must be formalized to ensure that unrelated restrictions do not remove u or v.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-node orbit fixing after binary branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-based replacement of the zero branch for a root-node binary-variable split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the root node, branch on a binary variable x_i with x_i=1 on the left and x_i=0 on the right. If j\in\operatorname{Orb}(i), then every feasible solution \widehat x in the right branch satisfying \widehat x_j=1 has an equivalent solution in the left branch. Consequently, the right branch may be strengthened to x_j=0 for every j\in\operatorname{Orb}(i).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After branching at the root on an orbit member, any right-branch solution that activates another member of the same orbit is symmetry-equivalent to a left-branch solution. Those solutions need not be searched again, so every variable in the orbit can be fixed to zero on the right branch.
assumptions_latex: x_i\in\{0,1\}\text{ and the root split is }x_i=1\text{ versus }x_i=0.
j\in\operatorname{Orb}(i)\text{ under model symmetries.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:x_i=0\}\text{ may be replaced, without losing an inequivalent solution, by }\{x:x_j=0\ \forall j\in\operatorname{Orb}(i)\}.

Ax\leq b.
